confirmedRules.name: Treasury-stock incremental shares for options and warrants
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: In-the-money options and warrants add only the shares left after the exercise proceeds are assumed to buy back stock at the current price; out-of-the-money ones add zero.
confirmedRules.given: 1,000,000 options outstanding with a weighted-average exercise price of $10.00 and a supplied price of $25.00
confirmedRules.when: the dilution bridge or a share-count scenario is computed
confirmedRules.then: incremental shares = 1,000,000 x (1 - 10/25) = 600,000 (rounded half-up to whole shares). At a price of $9.00 the result is 0.
confirmedRules.parameters: Formula count x (1 - strike/price) when price > strike, else 0; rounding floor(x+0.5)
edgeCases: Strike equal to price gives 0 (strict >)
When exercise-price-range tranches are tagged, each tranche is priced separately and summed; otherwise one weighted-average strike stands in, with a note
No strike tagged: method not_computed, incrementalShares null (unresolved)
Options tagged only on award/plan axes are summed across members; a single strike is used only when there is exactly one member

confirmedRules.name: If-converted shares for convertible notes
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Convertible notes count as shares when the price is at or above the conversion price. The share count comes from the tagged shares-issuable figure, otherwise principal/1000 x conversion ratio, otherwise principal / conversion price.
confirmedRules.given: $300,000,000 principal, conversion price $50.00, no shares-issuable tag and no usable ratio
confirmedRules.then: if-converted shares = 300,000,000 / 50 = 6,000,000; incremental = 6,000,000 at $50.00 (price >= conversion price) and 0 at $49.99
confirmedRules.parameters: Order: shares_issuable_tagged_at_period_end > principal/1000 x ratio > principal / conversion price. Implied conversion price = 1000 / ratio when only the ratio is tagged (rounded to 4 dp)
edgeCases: Principal outstanding at period end is preferred. A carrying amount is used only if it is below 95% of face (_REDUCED_PRINCIPAL_SHARE = 0.95); then face amount; then fallback concepts
Shares unknown means incremental null (unresolved instrument)
A redemption after period end (tagged on a subsequent-event axis) only raises a warning; shares are still counted as of the period end

confirmedRules.name: Conversion ratio unit normalization
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A tagged conversion ratio is trusted only if it agrees with the conversion price (shares per $1,000). A ratio tagged per $1 is scaled by 1,000. A ratio that matches neither is rejected.
confirmedRules.given: Tagged ratio 0.0076319 and conversion price $131.03
confirmedRules.then: 0.0076319 x 131.03 is about 1.000, which is within 2% of 1, so the ratio is scaled to 7.6319 per $1,000 (note RATIO_PER_1_PRINCIPAL_SCALED). A ratio of 2.6926 against $194.97 (product/1000 = 0.525) is RATIO_INCONSISTENT_WITH_PRICE and not used.
confirmedRules.parameters: _RATIO_PRICE_TOLERANCE = 0.02; per-1000 check |ratio x price / 1000 - 1| <= 0.02; per-1 check |ratio x price - 1| <= 0.02
edgeCases: No conversion price: a ratio >= 1 is accepted, a ratio < 1 is RATIO_UNIT_UNCERTAIN and not used
Ratio <= 0 or missing is not usable

confirmedRules.name: Net-share settlement when principal is stated as cash-settled
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If the filing says note principal must be paid in cash, conversion delivers shares only for the value above principal: if-converted shares minus principal / price, floored at zero.
confirmedRules.given: A note with 6,000,000 if-converted shares, $300,000,000 principal, conversion price $50, and a filing sentence 'principal ... must be settled in cash'
confirmedRules.then: net-share settlement shares = max(0, 6,000,000 - 300,000,000/75) = 2,000,000. Out of the money (price < $50) gives 0.
confirmedRules.parameters: Settlement sentence must match _CASH_PRINCIPAL_RE and must NOT contain optional wording (may/can/at our option)
edgeCases: The scope can be ALL_NOTES, NAMED_NOTES (matched by year in the instrument name), or UNNAMED_NOTES (used only when there is exactly one note)
Principal untagged gives null (unresolved)
The EPS-basis dilutedSharesAtPrice still uses full if-converted; the net figure is reported alongside it

confirmedRules.name: Capped call economic offset
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A stated capped call reduces shares by covered x (min(price, cap) - strike) / price. It is computed only when the strike, the cap and the covered shares are all stated, and it is never part of the EPS count.
confirmedRules.given: Capped call strike $50, cap $80, 6,000,000 covered shares
confirmedRules.parameters: A stated covered count is used if it is at most 1.01 x the notes' current if-converted shares, or if the filing says the capped calls survived conversions; otherwise the notes' shares bound it
edgeCases: The strike can be taken as the conversion price when the text says it corresponds to it
Missing terms give unresolvedReason CAPPED_CALL_TERMS_INCOMPLETE with missingTerms
In share scenarios it applies only when capped_calls = offset_when_stated

confirmedRules.name: Diluted share count and dilution percentage at price
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Diluted shares = basic shares + incremental options + unvested awards (gross) + warrants + convertibles + convertible preferred. Dilution % = (diluted - basic) / basic x 100.
confirmedRules.given: Basic 100,000,000; options +600,000; awards +2,000,000; warrants +1,400,000; convertibles +4,000,000; preferred 0
confirmedRules.then: dilutedSharesAtPrice = 108,000,000; dilutionPctAtPrice = 8.00%. Gross dilution adds every outstanding instrument regardless of moneyness.
confirmedRules.parameters: Rounding half-up: shares to 0 dp, percentages to 2 dp. Variants: NetShareSettlement, NetOfCappedCalls, WithAtm
edgeCases: Basic shares come from the cover page (undimensioned, else sum of per-class counts at the latest date), else the balance-sheet CommonStockSharesOutstanding
No basic shares gives status NOT_FOUND, bridge null
Basic <= 0 gives a null percentage
An unresolved component is treated as 0 in the sum but makes status PARTIAL

confirmedRules.name: Dilution bridge status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The bridge is COMPUTED only when every tagged component resolved and no unquantified share claim is open. Otherwise it is PARTIAL, and NOT_FOUND when there is no basic share count.
confirmedRules.given: A filing where warrants have an untagged exercise price
confirmedRules.then: warrants are listed in 'unresolved' and status = PARTIAL
confirmedRules.parameters: Open claim statuses: UNQUANTIFIED, REPORTED_NOT_MODELED
edgeCases: Partial means a component resolved with unresolvedClasses or unresolvedInstruments > 0
COMPUTED never means a full claim inventory

confirmedRules.name: ATM program potential shares
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The remaining at-the-market capacity stated in filing text, divided by the price, gives the potential shares. Amounts under $100,000 are ignored as unscaled.
confirmedRules.given: Filing text 'approximately $150 million remains available under the ATM program' and a price of $25
confirmedRules.then: potentialShares = 150,000,000 / 25 = 6,000,000 (shown separately; not in dilutedSharesAtPrice)
confirmedRules.parameters: Minimum amount 100,000; clause classifier keywords: remaining/available/unsold, sold/issued/proceeds, up to/aggregate offering price; scale words billion/bn, million/mm/m, thousand/k
edgeCases: Only program size stated: not_computed, potentialShares null
The first remaining-capacity sentence found wins

confirmedRules.name: Convertible preferred if-converted and liquidation preference
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Convertible preferred counts its tagged issuable common shares when price >= conversion price. A ratio stated in text with no conversion price counts as converted at any price. The liquidation preference is the tagged aggregate, else per-share x preferred shares outstanding.
confirmedRules.given: 2,000,000 preferred shares, 21,800,000 issuable common shares, conversion price $91.84, liquidation preference $500.00 per share
confirmedRules.then: incremental = 21,800,000; liquidation preference = 500 x 2,000,000 = $1,000,000,000; at $90 incremental = 0
confirmedRules.parameters: Preferred outstanding = the larger of PreferredStockSharesOutstanding and TemporaryEquitySharesOutstanding (never summed); dividend rate x 100, rounded to 4 dp
edgeCases: No conversion price and no text ratio: incremental null (unresolved)
countBeforePeriodEnd flag when the issuable count predates the period end

confirmedRules.name: Warrant count vs company-reported antidilutive table
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The bridge's warrant shares are flagged if they differ from the company's antidilutive-securities table by more than 5% or 100,000 shares, whichever is larger.
confirmedRules.given: The bridge counts 10,000,000 warrant shares; the company's table reports 12,000,000
confirmedRules.then: |12,000,000 - 10,000,000| = 2,000,000 > max(600,000, 100,000), so warning WARRANT_COUNT_DIFFERS_FROM_REPORTED
confirmedRules.parameters: Relative 5%; absolute floor 100,000 shares
edgeCases: The table may be a weighted average, so the result is a warning only

confirmedRules.name: Enterprise value in valuation snapshot
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: EV = price x diluted shares + total debt - convertible principal already counted as shares + preferred liquidation preference not counted as shares - cash - short-term investments.
confirmedRules.given: Price $25, diluted shares 108,000,000, debt $500M, in-the-money convertible principal $300M, no preferred, cash $400M, short-term investments $100M
confirmedRules.then: equity value = $2,700M; EV = 2,700 + 500 - 300 + 0 - 400 - 100 = $2,400M (rounded half-up to whole units). Status is COMPUTED when EV exists, else PARTIAL.
confirmedRules.parameters: The convertible adjustment is capped at total debt. Short-term investments are used only with SEC balances (Yahoo's cash already includes them)
edgeCases: Missing shares, cash or debt gives ENTERPRISE_VALUE_INCOMPLETE
Balances in a different currency from the quote give ENTERPRISE_VALUE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH and no EV
Preferred with no tagged liquidation preference is left out, with warning PREFERRED_NOT_IN_ENTERPRISE_VALUE
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The convertible-principal deduction (valuation.py:373-377) is not gated on sec_usable, unlike the preferred adjustment (line 382). When SHARE_BASIS_MISMATCH falls back to Yahoo basic shares (no convertible shares counted), debt is still reduced by convertible principal, which understates EV.

confirmedRules.name: ADR ordinary-shares-per-quoted-share ratio
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For foreign filers (20-F/40-F only), when SEC ordinary shares are within 2% of a whole multiple (2x or more) of Yahoo's quoted shares, SEC counts are divided by that multiple before the price is applied.
confirmedRules.given: A 20-F filer with 25,930,380,000 SEC ordinary shares and 5,186,076,000 Yahoo shares
confirmedRules.then: ratio r = 5.000, which rounds to n = 5 with |r - 5| <= 0.10, so the ADR ratio is 5 (ADR_RATIO_APPLIED) and SEC shares are divided by 5
confirmedRules.parameters: _ADS_MIN_RATIO = 1.9; _ADS_RATIO_TOLERANCE = 0.02 x n; inverse ratios (r <= 1/1.9) give 1/k
edgeCases: Domestic (10-K) filers are never treated as ADRs, even near 2x
No whole multiple and r > 1.5 or r < 1/1.5: SHARE_BASIS_MISMATCH, and Yahoo's count is used

confirmedRules.name: Yahoo implied all-class share count substitution
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Yahoo's implied shares outstanding replaces the listed-class count when it is more than 2% larger (or the listed count is missing).
confirmedRules.given: Listed shares 300,000,000; implied shares 310,000,000
confirmedRules.when: the Yahoo share basis is chosen
confirmedRules.then: 310,000,000 > 306,000,000, so implied shares are used (shareBasis yahoo_implied_shares_outstanding); with implied 305,000,000 the listed count is used
confirmedRules.parameters: _IMPLIED_SHARES_MIN_RATIO = 1.02
edgeCases: No share count at all: market cap is taken from Yahoo marketCap

confirmedRules.name: SEC vs Yahoo balance-sheet source selection and staleness
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Filing period-end cash and debt are preferred. They give way to Yahoo when they are in another currency than the quote, or more than 45 days older than Yahoo's latest quarter while Yahoo has both cash and debt.
confirmedRules.given: SEC balances as of 2025-12-31, Yahoo most recent quarter 2026-03-31, Yahoo cash and debt present
confirmedRules.then: 90 days > 45, so Yahoo's cash/debt are used (SEC_BALANCES_STALE warning, plus YAHOO_BALANCES info)
confirmedRules.parameters: _STALE_BALANCE_DAYS = 45
edgeCases: If Yahoo lacks cash or debt, the stale SEC balances are still used, with a warning
SEC balances require both totalDebt and cashAndEquivalents
Capital-structure warnings travel with SEC balances

confirmedRules.name: SEC/Yahoo cash mismatch and shortfall checks
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Two warnings. (1) SEC cash alone matches Yahoo's total cash within 2%, but cash plus short-term investments is more than 10% above it (possible double count). (2) Same quarter (within 7 days), Yahoo cash is more than 5% above SEC cash plus investments.
confirmedRules.given: SEC cash $1,000M, SEC short-term investments $200M, Yahoo total cash $1,010M
confirmedRules.then: 1,200 > 1.10 x 1,010 = 1,111 and |1,000 - 1,010| = 10 <= 20.2, so SEC_YAHOO_CASH_MISMATCH. Separately, Yahoo $1,100M vs SEC $1,000M same quarter: 1,100 > 1,050, so SEC_YAHOO_CASH_SHORTFALL
confirmedRules.parameters: _SEC_YAHOO_EXCESS = 0.10; _SEC_YAHOO_CASH_MATCH = 0.02; _SEC_YAHOO_SHORTFALL = 0.05; _SAME_QUARTER_DAYS = 7
edgeCases: Flagged only, never overridden
Skipped when currencies are not comparable

confirmedRules.name: Minor-unit quote conversion and currency comparability
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Quotes in pence, cents or agorot are divided by 100 into the major currency. Financials are combined with the quote only when the financial currency equals the major quote currency (or either is unknown).
confirmedRules.given: A quote of 1,250 GBp with financialCurrency GBP
confirmedRules.when: the snapshot or peer row is computed
confirmedRules.then: major price = GBP 12.50 and currencies are comparable; a USD quote with TWD financials is not comparable, so multiples are 'not computed'
confirmedRules.parameters: GBp/GBX -> GBP /100; ZAc -> ZAR /100; ILA -> ILS /100
edgeCases: Unknown currency on either side is treated as comparable

confirmedRules.name: Valuation multiples and denominators
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: EV/Revenue (TTM, current FY, next FY consensus), EV/EBITDA (TTM) and P/E (trailing EPS, current and next FY consensus EPS) are numerator / denominator, rounded half-up to 2 dp. They are blank when the denominator is zero or negative, or the currencies differ.
confirmedRules.given: EV $2,400M and TTM revenue $800M; price $25 and trailing EPS -$0.40
confirmedRules.then: EV/Revenue TTM = 3.00x; P/E TTM = null with note 'Denominator is zero or negative'
confirmedRules.parameters: Rounding 2 dp half-up; periods 0y = current_fiscal_year, +1y = next_fiscal_year
edgeCases: Analyst counts are carried for consensus denominators
Not comparable currency: all multiples null

confirmedRules.name: Consensus revenue growth percentages
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Current-FY consensus revenue vs TTM revenue, and next-FY vs current-FY consensus, as percentage growth.
confirmedRules.given: TTM revenue $800M, FY0 consensus $1,000M, FY+1 consensus $1,250M
confirmedRules.then: currentFiscalYearVsTtmPct = 25.00; nextVsCurrentFiscalYearPct = 25.00
confirmedRules.parameters: (a/b - 1) x 100, 2 dp half-up; requires b > 0
edgeCases: Null when the base is missing or <= 0

confirmedRules.name: Peer medians and subject premium
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Peer medians, min and max exclude the subject. The subject's premium = (own / median - 1) x 100, not computed for percentage metrics or a non-positive median. Requests need 2-10 distinct tickers including the subject.
confirmedRules.given: Peer EV/Revenue TTM values 2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0 and subject 7.5
confirmedRules.parameters: _PEER_VALUATION_MAX_TICKERS = 10; minimum 2; metrics: evToRevenueTtm/CurrentFy/NextFy, evToEbitdaTtm, peCurrentFy, peNextFy, revenueGrowthNextFyPct, grossMarginPct
edgeCases: Metrics ending in 'Pct' get no premium
Every peer uses the Yahoo basis (price x Yahoo shares + debt - cash)

confirmedRules.name: Share-count scenario input validation and defaults
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A call takes 1 to 8 scenarios, each with a unique name of 1-60 characters and a positive price. Each treatment must come from an allowed list and defaults when omitted. Each scenario takes at most 10 known-issuance rows with a label and positive shares.
confirmedRules.given: A scenario {name:'Bull', price:40} with no treatments
confirmedRules.then: treatments default to options=treasury_stock, unvested_awards=gross, warrants=treasury_stock, warrant_vesting=vested_only, convertibles=if_converted_when_in_the_money, atm=exclude, capped_calls=ignore, and all 7 are listed as defaulted
confirmedRules.parameters: SHARE_SCENARIO_LIMIT = 8; name max 60; _KNOWN_ISSUANCE_LIMIT = 10; label truncated to 120, source to 300
edgeCases: A repeated name is an error
Price <= 0 or non-numeric is an error

confirmedRules.name: Scenario resulting shares, dilution and completeness
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Resulting shares = basic + included incremental shares + caller-declared known issuance. The completeness label follows a fixed precedence.
confirmedRules.given: Basic 100,000,000, included instrument increments 5,000,000, known issuance 1,000,000
confirmedRules.then: resultingShares = 106,000,000; dilutionPct = 6.00. The status is COMPUTED only if every scenario is TAGGED_INSTRUMENTS_RESOLVED
confirmedRules.parameters: Completeness order: NO_BASIC_SHARES > EXCLUDES_UNRESOLVED_INSTRUMENTS > EXCLUDES_UNQUANTIFIED_CLAIMS > CLAIM_TEXT_NOT_READ > TAGGED_INSTRUMENTS_RESOLVED
edgeCases: Unresolved instruments are left out of the total
A warrant class with vesting conditions but no exercisable count is not assumed fully exercisable
ATM full_remaining_capacity = remaining / price

confirmedRules.name: Funding text amount parsing and range rule
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The first dollar amount (or a low-to-high range) is read from a sentence. A figure under $100,000 with no scale word is SCALE_NOT_STATED rather than taken at face value, and two amounts form a range only when joined by to/-/and and ascending.
confirmedRules.given: 'We expect capital expenditures of $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion in 2026'
confirmedRules.then: low = 1,200,000,000; high = 1,500,000,000; qualifier 'range'. '$550.0' alone gives SCALE_NOT_STATED; 'committed $1.2 billion and $300 million' is not a range (descending)
confirmedRules.parameters: Scale threshold 100,000; qualifiers up_to / approximately / range / stated; per-share/unit amounts skipped
edgeCases: The scale word of either end applies to the other when one is missing

confirmedRules.name: Funding/capex sentence classification precedence
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Sentences are classified in this order: reported-period spending (REPORTED_ACTUAL, unless also forward-looking), then grants/incentives (AWARDED_CONTINGENT), then commitments (COMPANY_DISCLOSED_COMMITTED), then expects/plans (COMPANY_GUIDED), else UNRESOLVED. A sentence with no amount is UNRESOLVED.
confirmedRules.given: 'Purchase obligations of approximately $2.93 billion are expected to be paid within one year'
confirmedRules.then: COMPANY_DISCLOSED_COMMITTED (a commitment beats the forward-looking word), amount 2.93e9 approximately, timing UNSTATED
confirmedRules.parameters: Sentence length 40-1,200 chars; sentences ending ';' skipped; at most 25 items; 'net of government incentives' is not an award; equity-award wording is not contingent funding
edgeCases: No amount and no strong keyword: dropped
Duplicate sentences (first 200 chars) are skipped

confirmedRules.name: Contractual obligation bucket dates
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Tagged debt, lease, purchase and contractual obligation buckets get a 'period through' date = period end + N years for buckets 1-5. Purchase commitments tagged with a min/max range axis are reported as a low-high range.
confirmedRules.given: Period end 2025-12-31 and a tagged year_3 debt maturity
confirmedRules.then: periodThrough = 2028-12-31; remainder_of_fiscal_year and after_year_5 get null
confirmedRules.parameters: Offsets 0..6; only undimensioned facts at the period end
edgeCases: The first concept per bucket wins (purchase vs unrecorded obligation)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: _add_years does string arithmetic on the year, so a 2024-02-29 period end produces the invalid date 2025-02-29 (same in worker addYears and capital_structure.py:2537-2538); server.py:11955-11960 handles Feb 29 correctly.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should a Feb-29 period end roll to Feb-28 for bucket 'period through' dates?

confirmedRules.name: Fiscal year of a 52/53-week period end
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A period's fiscal year is the calendar year of the date 7 days before its end, so a year ending in the first week of January belongs to the prior year.
confirmedRules.given: A fiscal year ending 2027-01-02
confirmedRules.when: the fiscal year label is computed
confirmedRules.parameters: WEEK_DRIFT_DAYS = 7
edgeCases: Company naming offsets (e.g. DG) are applied separately
An invalid date gives null

confirmedRules.name: Fiscal quarter from distance to year end
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The quarter = 4 - round(days to fiscal year end / 91), accepted only within 10 days of a quarter boundary and within the year.
confirmedRules.given: Quarter end 2026-06-27, fiscal year end 2026-12-26 (182 days)
confirmedRules.then: round(182/91) = 2, so Q2
confirmedRules.parameters: Gap window -7..280 days; boundary tolerance 7+3 = 10 days; 91 days per quarter
edgeCases: Off-boundary or out-of-year periods give null

confirmedRules.name: Fiscal calendar rule detection and projection
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: From two or more annual period ends, the rule is kept only if it reproduces every one: month end; otherwise weekday nearest month end (within ±3 days) and/or last such weekday of the month. A date is projected only when the fitting rules agree.
confirmedRules.given: Year ends 2026-01-30, 2025-01-31, 2024-02-02 (Fridays nearest Jan 31)
confirmedRules.when: the calendar is fitted and a provider date of 2027-01-31 is mapped
confirmedRules.then: pattern WEEKDAY_NEAREST_MONTH_END, Friday, so the company year end is 2027-01-29
confirmedRules.parameters: Look-back adds older ends until one pattern remains or one fails
edgeCases: Different nominal months gives no calendar
Two rules disagreeing for the target year gives null

confirmedRules.name: Company fiscal-year naming offset
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The company's own fiscal-year numbering is learned from its latest 3 annual reports (fy stated vs period-end rule). It applies only if all agree and the offset is at most ±1 year. A filing's own DocumentFiscalYearFocus is trusted when within 1 year of the rule.
confirmedRules.given: DG's 10-Ks state fy 2025 for the year ending 2026-01-30 (rule says 2026) in all 3 recent reports
confirmedRules.then: offset = -1, basis SEC_STATED_FISCAL_YEAR, so FY0 consensus is labeled FY2025
confirmedRules.parameters: _NAMING_REPORTS = 3; annual duration 350-380 days; |offset| <= 1
edgeCases: Disagreement gives offset 0 with basis PERIOD_END_RULE_STATED_YEARS_INCONSISTENT
No companyfacts: PERIOD_END_RULE_SEC_NOT_READ

confirmedRules.name: Earnings release fiscal period extraction
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A release's fiscal period is read only from one phrase that joins a quarter to a year (e.g. 'fourth quarter of fiscal 2026', 'Q4 FY2026'). The earliest such phrase wins, and it is never inferred from the filing date.
confirmedRules.given: Release text 'Micron Technology reports results for the fourth quarter and full year of fiscal 2026 ...'
confirmedRules.then: period = 'FY2026 Q4', periodStatus EX99_TEXT_RESOLVED; no match gives UNRESOLVED
confirmedRules.parameters: Year-before-quarter pattern allows at most 40 characters without sentence/dash breaks
edgeCases: Comparative prior-year phrases later in the text are ignored

confirmedRules.name: Latest annual report missing from SEC companyfacts
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Warn LATEST_ANNUAL_NOT_IN_COMPANYFACTS when the newest 10-K/20-F/40-F filed by the as-of date contributes no us-gaap or ifrs-full fact and no held annual period reaches its report date.
confirmedRules.given: TSM's FY2025 20-F (report date 2025-12-31) with no financial facts; companyfacts' newest annual period ends 2024-12-31
confirmedRules.then: warning raised; figures are understood to come from FY2024
confirmedRules.parameters: Annual forms 10-K, 20-F, 40-F (amendments excluded when choosing latest filing; /A accepted for held-period check)
edgeCases: An amendment that put the year into companyfacts suppresses the warning
Ties on filing date are broken by accession number

confirmedRules.name: Metric reconciliation tolerance and match
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each source matches the latest SEC value if |difference| <= max(SEC value x tolerance%, half the last stated digit of a release figure). The default tolerance is 0.5%, clamped to 0-10%.
confirmedRules.given: SEC revenue $31,512,000; release says '$31.5 million'
confirmedRules.then: release precision = 0.5 x 10^-1 x 1,000,000 = $50,000; tolerance = max(157,560, 50,000) = $157,560; difference -12,000, so MATCH; differencePct = -0.0381
confirmedRules.parameters: DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_PCT = 0.5; clamp [0,10]; epsilon 1e-9 x max(1,|b|); difference rounded to 6 dp, pct to 4 dp
edgeCases: As-first-filed vs latest SEC mismatch gives RESTATED, not a conflict
Without SEC, sources are compared with the first found and can never be AGREED

confirmedRules.name: Metric reconciliation status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: NOT_FOUND if no source found the value; CONFLICT if any non-SEC source mismatches; PARTIAL if there is no SEC baseline or only one provider; AGREED needs the latest SEC value plus at least one matching independent provider.
confirmedRules.given: SEC and Yahoo both found revenue within tolerance; release not found
confirmedRules.then: AGREED, providersAgreeingWithSec = ['YAHOO'], independentChecks = 1
confirmedRules.parameters: Providers read: SEC, ISSUER_RELEASE, YAHOO; Alpha Vantage never read
edgeCases: A restatement alone does not cause CONFLICT
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The worker tool description (worker/src/tools.ts:557) says 'AGREED (two or more providers agree)', while the Python description (server.py:10742) and both codepaths require a latest-SEC baseline. This breaks the documented parity.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Confirm AGREED always requires the SEC baseline, so the worker tool description should be corrected.

confirmedRules.name: Release figure selection when multiple releases are read
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Of the releases read for a period (oldest first), the chosen observation is the last one with a scoped figure. If none has one, the first release read is used.
confirmedRules.given: Two releases: the original (FOUND $31.5M) and a later re-release (FOUND $31.6M)
confirmedRules.then: code selects the later one ($31.6M)
confirmedRules.parameters: _RELEASE_READ_MAX = 4 (server.py:10715)
edgeCases: All releases are listed in releasesConsidered
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The docstring says 'the first with a scoped figure' but the code takes found[-1] (the newest). Both runtimes match each other but contradict the documentation.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should reconciliation use the earliest release figure (as originally reported) or the latest re-release?

confirmedRules.name: Reconciliation release-sentence scoping and scale
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A release figure is accepted only from a sentence that names the metric, is not guidance, backlog, non-GAAP or per-share (for money metrics), and matches the period scope. Unscaled figures take the release's table scale only if exactly one is declared.
confirmedRules.given: A release with '(in thousands, except per share data)' and the sentence 'Revenue for the fourth quarter was $1,214,293'
confirmedRules.when: the release is read for the latest quarter
confirmedRules.then: value = 1,214,293 x 1,000 = $1,214,293,000 with scaleBasis RELEASE_TABLE_IN_THOUSANDS; '(loss)' or parentheses make the value negative
confirmedRules.parameters: Sentence max 600 chars; scale words b/bn/billion, m/mm/mn/million, k/thousand
edgeCases: Several table scales declared: unscaled figure rejected
Non-USD reporting unit: NOT_COMPARED_CURRENCY

confirmedRules.name: Reconciliation period resolution
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Quarters are 80-100 day periods and years are 350-380 days. 'Q<n> yyyy' is the calendar quarter of the period end. 'FY yyyy' prefers the issuer's SEC fy/fp. Without metadata the fiscal quarter is counted from the prior year end as round(days / 91.25), clamped 1-4.
confirmedRules.given: spec 'Q3 2026' and a revenue quarter 2026-04-27 to 2026-07-26
confirmedRules.then: ceil(7/3) = 3, so it matches; fiscal quarter from first-filed fy/fp (e.g. FY2027 Q2)
confirmedRules.parameters: Quarter 80-100 days; annual 350-380 days; 91.25 days per quarter
edgeCases: A prior year end in Jan-Mar gives two candidate fiscal years, flagged fiscalYearAmbiguous
20-F/40-F filers have no quarters

confirmedRules.name: Parent net income derived from ProfitLoss
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a filer tags only ProfitLoss, net income = ProfitLoss - NetIncomeLossAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest from the same filing and period.
confirmedRules.given: ProfitLoss $120M and NCI $8M in the same accession
confirmedRules.then: value = $112M, basis PARENT_DERIVED_FROM_PROFITLOSS
confirmedRules.parameters: Revenue tagged under two concepts in one filing: the larger magnitude wins
edgeCases: NCI missing for either filing: ProfitLoss used as is

confirmedRules.name: Reporting unit choice for a metric
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The reporting currency is the unit filed most recently, then the one with the most facts, then alphabetical. The historical engine uses the newest annual revenue unit filed by each date.
confirmedRules.given: NBIS with RUB facts to FY2023 and USD from FY2024
confirmedRules.then: USD is chosen (newest filing), despite the longer RUB history
confirmedRules.parameters: Money unit regex [A-Z]{3}; per-share [A-Z]{3}/shares
edgeCases: Convenience translations: the main currency wins if present

confirmedRules.name: Consensus curve policy inputs
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: horizon_years must be an integer 1-5, min_analyst_count an integer 1-50, and conflict_tolerance_pct 0-100. EPS also has a fixed absolute tolerance of $0.02.
confirmedRules.given: horizon_years=7
confirmedRules.then: INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR 'horizon_years must be an integer from 1 to 5.'
confirmedRules.parameters: Defaults horizonYears 5, minAnalystCount 3, conflictTolerancePct 10, epsAbsoluteTolerance 0.02
edgeCases: Non-numeric input gives a single combined error

confirmedRules.name: Consensus provider agreement
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For each fiscal year and metric, provider means are compared. The relative diff = (high - low) / max(|high|, |low|) x 100. It is AGREED if within the tolerance (or EPS within $0.02), else CONFLICT.
confirmedRules.given: Yahoo FY0 EPS mean 5.20 and Alpha Vantage 5.00
confirmedRules.then: absolute 0.20 > 0.02; relative = 0.20/5.20 x 100 = 3.85% <= 10%, so AGREED
confirmedRules.parameters: Fiscal-year-end spread > 10 days gives PERIOD_IDENTITY_MISMATCH; differing currencies give CURRENCY_MISMATCH; identical at the coarsest published precision with equal analyst counts gives IDENTICAL (NOT_INDEPENDENT)
edgeCases: A single usable provider gives SINGLE_PROVIDER
Inconsistent rows are excluded and named

confirmedRules.name: Provider row consistency and coverage state
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A row whose mean is above its high, below its low, or whose low exceeds its high is PROVIDER_INCONSISTENT. A row with fewer analysts than the minimum (default 3) is INSUFFICIENT_ANALYST_COUNT.
confirmedRules.given: Alpha Vantage revenue mean 667.6M with high 652.7M
confirmedRules.then: state PROVIDER_INCONSISTENT (MEAN_ABOVE_HIGH), excluded from agreement, warning PROVIDER_ROW_INCONSISTENT
confirmedRules.parameters: Tolerance 1e-9 x max(1,|v|); highLowRangePctOfMean = (high - low)/|mean| x 100, 2 dp
edgeCases: An analyst count of 0 nulls out mean/high/low

confirmedRules.name: EPS gap explained by an unadjusted stock split
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When two same-sign EPS means conflict and their ratio is within 15% of a split factor (>= 1.5) from the last 400 days, the cell is NOT_SPLIT_ADJUSTED rather than CONFLICT.
confirmedRules.given: Provider A EPS 2.73 and B 0.73, with a 4-for-1 split 120 days ago
confirmedRules.then: gap 3.74; |3.74/4 - 1| = 6.5% <= 15%, so NOT_SPLIT_ADJUSTED, provider A (the larger value) flagged not adjusted
confirmedRules.parameters: SPLIT_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 400; SPLIT_RATIO_TOLERANCE = 0.15; min factor 1.5; cumulative product of multiple splits also tested
edgeCases: Reverse split: the smaller-magnitude provider is flagged
Exactly two providers required

confirmedRules.name: FY0 resolution and fiscal-year offset
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: FY0 is Yahoo's '0y' fiscal year end, else the earliest provider year end on or after today. Other years are placed by round(days apart / 365.25).
confirmedRules.given: FY0 end 2026-12-31 and an Alpha Vantage row ending 2028-12-31
confirmedRules.then: offset = round(731/365.25) = 2, so FY+2
confirmedRules.parameters: 365.25 days per year; yfinance FY0 end = nextFiscalYearEnd, +1y = +1 calendar year (Feb 29 goes to Feb 28)
edgeCases: No year end stated: NO_PROVIDER_FISCAL_YEAR

confirmedRules.name: Stale provider snapshot fallback
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When Alpha Vantage refuses a request for rate limit, timeout or provider error, the newest stored payload up to 7 days old stands in, marked stale with its age in hours. A good payload is stored at most once a day.
confirmedRules.given: A live RATE_LIMIT at 2026-10-14T12:00Z and a snapshot fetched 2026-10-13T05:30Z
confirmedRules.then: the snapshot is used, ageHours = 30.5, warning PROVIDER_DATA_STALE
confirmedRules.parameters: STALE_FALLBACK_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7; statuses RATE_LIMIT, TIMEOUT, PROVIDER_ERROR; Alpha Vantage cache TTL 86,400 s
edgeCases: Missing key or entitlement never falls back
A future-dated snapshot is rejected

confirmedRules.name: EPS revision windows
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For the 7/30/60/90-day windows, change = current - past mean and change% = change / |past| x 100. A window containing a split (plus 1 day margin) or an inconsistent row carries no change.
confirmedRules.given: Current EPS mean 5.20, 30-day-ago mean 5.00, no splits
confirmedRules.then: 30d change = 0.20, changePct = 4.00, state COMPARED
confirmedRules.parameters: Windows 7, 30, 60, 90 days; split look-back 91 days
edgeCases: Past mean 0: changePct null
Revenue revisions and analyst adds/drops are PROVIDER_NOT_COVERED

confirmedRules.name: Evidence quality freshness thresholds
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A quote is STALE after 4 days. A periodic SEC filing is STALE after 135 days (quarterly filers) or 492 days (20-F/40-F). Earnings guidance is STALE more than 120 days after the last 8-K Item 2.02. Failed provider calls are UNAVAILABLE and retryable, not missing.
confirmedRules.given: A 10-Q for period 2026-03-31 checked on 2026-08-20
confirmedRules.then: age 142 days > 135, so secPeriodicFiling STALE, blocker SEC_PERIODIC_STALE
confirmedRules.parameters: QUARTERLY_REPORT_STALE_DAYS = 135; ANNUAL_REPORT_STALE_DAYS = 365+120+7 = 492; quote 4 days; guidance 120 days; 8-K window 90 days
edgeCases: Consensus READY only when every FY0/FY+1 cell is PROVIDER_COVERED
All providers failed gives CONSENSUS_PROVIDER_ERROR

confirmedRules.name: LTM and LFY flow figures
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: LFY is the latest 350-380 day period. LTM = LFY + current year-to-date - prior-year year-to-date, or LFY itself when nothing later is filed.
confirmedRules.then: LTM = 1,000 + 900 - 750 = $1,150M (method LFY_PLUS_YTD_MINUS_PRIOR_YTD)
confirmedRules.parameters: YTD must start 0-4 days after LFY end; prior YTD start within 4 days of LFY start, end 358-372 days before YTD end, span within 7 days
edgeCases: Missing YTD gives YEAR_TO_DATE_NOT_FILED
Missing prior YTD gives PRIOR_YEAR_TO_DATE_NOT_FILED

confirmedRules.name: Point-in-time price with later splits undone
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A date's price is the last close within 7 days on or before it, multiplied by all later split ratios so it matches the share count reported at the time.
confirmedRules.given: An adjusted close of $30 on 2023-06-30 and a 4-for-1 split on 2024-06-10
confirmedRules.parameters: 7-day look-back; minor units converted to major
edgeCases: No close within 7 days: PRICE_UNAVAILABLE
A split between the share-count date and the trading date gives SPLIT_AFTER_SHARE_COUNT and no market cap

confirmedRules.name: Historical market cap, EV and multiples
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Market cap = price x point-in-time shares (divided by the ADS ratio). EV = market cap + (debt - cash - short-term investments) x FX. Multiples need a positive numerator and FX-converted denominator, rounded to 2 dp.
confirmedRules.given: Price $120, 50,000,000 shares, debt $800M, cash $300M, STI $100M, FX 1, LTM revenue $1,150M
confirmedRules.then: market cap = $6,000M; EV = 6,000 + 400 = $6,400M; EV/Revenue LTM = 5.57
confirmedRules.parameters: Weighted-average shares never set market cap; a share count <= 0 is rejected; EBITDA = operating income + D&A for the same period end
edgeCases: Negative EV: NOT_MEANINGFUL_NONPOSITIVE_NUMERATOR
Net loss: NOT_MEANINGFUL_NONPOSITIVE_DENOMINATOR
No borrowing concept tagged in the cash filing: debt = 0 (NO_BORROWINGS_TAGGED)

confirmedRules.name: Historical staleness limits by filer cadence
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Quarterly (10-K/10-Q) filers: share counts stale after 400 days, balances after 200, results after 500. Annual 20-F/40-F filers: 500 days for all, with an info flag when the share count is older than 183 days.
confirmedRules.given: A 10-K filer whose latest balance sheet is 230 days before the date
confirmedRules.then: BALANCES_STALE, EV null
confirmedRules.parameters: QUARTERLY shareCount 400, balances 200, results 500; ANNUAL 500/500/500; SHARE_COUNT_AGED_DAYS = 183
edgeCases: Cadence is judged per date from the latest annual form filed by then

confirmedRules.name: Historical valuation dates and peers
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: At most 12 requested dates in YYYY-MM-DD form. The default is the latest close and its 5 prior anniversaries (Feb 29 goes to Feb 28). At most 5 peers, whose medians are unweighted.
confirmedRules.given: Latest close 2024-02-29 and no dates requested
confirmedRules.parameters: MAX_DATES = 12; max peers 5; peers fetched 3 at a time; median rounded to 2 dp
edgeCases: Duplicate dates are de-duplicated and sorted

confirmedRules.name: Total debt concept hierarchy and finance-lease removal
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Debt = LongTermDebt (else current + noncurrent) plus short-term borrowings, plus separately reported convertibles if larger. Otherwise lease-inclusive totals less the finance-lease liability. Otherwise the sum of debt lines.
confirmedRules.given: A filer tagging DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations $5,722M and FinanceLeaseLiability $2,670M
confirmedRules.then: total debt = 5,722 - 2,670 = $3,052M (leases SUBTRACTED)
confirmedRules.parameters: The lease is subtracted only if it is <= gross; DebtCurrent takes precedence over the current lease-inclusive line
edgeCases: No finance lease tagged: leases INCLUDED
No borrowing concept at all: the filing reports no borrowings

confirmedRules.name: Balance-sheet fact exclusion (rounded or overlapping cash)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A period-end fact tagged at least 2 decimal places coarser than the cash line, or whose sentence calls it cash equivalents/money-market and is no larger than cash, is not treated as a balance-sheet amount.
confirmedRules.given: Cash tagged with decimals -3 and an investments fact with decimals -8 ('approximately $2.3 billion')
confirmedRules.then: the investment fact is excluded as 'rounded'
confirmedRules.parameters: _ROUNDED_DECIMALS_GAP = 2
edgeCases: Dimensioned facts are always kept

confirmedRules.name: Price input validation for bridge and snapshot
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The dilution bridge needs a finite positive price. The snapshot price is optional but must be positive when supplied. SEC filings are read for the snapshot only when the listing's major currency is USD.
confirmedRules.given: price = 0
confirmedRules.then: INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR
confirmedRules.parameters: Bridge currency default USD
edgeCases: Non-USD listings get a NON_USD_LISTING info warning and Yahoo figures

confirmedRules.name: Ticker symbol format check
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A ticker is accepted only if, after trimming and upper-casing, it is 1 to 20 characters made of letters, digits or the characters . - ^ =.
confirmedRules.given: A caller passes ticker ' brk-b ' and another passes 'AAPL$'
confirmedRules.when: Any tool that validates tickers runs
confirmedRules.then: 'BRK-B' passes. 'AAPL$' is rejected with INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR: "Invalid ticker symbol: 'AAPL$'. Must be 1-20 characters: uppercase letters, digits, or . - ^ ="
confirmedRules.parameters: Pattern ^[A-Z0-9.\-\^=]{1,20}$; max length 20
edgeCases: Lower-case input is upper-cased before the check, so it passes
Empty string fails the check
The Worker runs this check only in get_historical_prices (worker/src/tools.ts:2024-2031). Python runs it in about 30 tools (server.py:2743, 3967, 4025, 8279, 11613 and others)

confirmedRules.name: SEC accession number format check
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An SEC accession number must have the form 10 digits, dash, 2 digits, dash, 6 digits.
confirmedRules.then: The first is accepted. The second is rejected with INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR 'Expected format: XXXXXXXXXX-YY-ZZZZZZ.'
edgeCases: Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped before matching
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: No equivalent accession-format check exists anywhere in worker/src/*.ts (grep found none), so the Worker diverges from Python.

confirmedRules.name: SEC document URLs restricted to the EDGAR Archives
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Any SEC document URL a caller supplies must start with https://www.sec.gov/Archives/. Other hosts and paths are refused.
confirmedRules.given: document_url 'https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?...'
confirmedRules.when: get_filing_section, list_filing_tables, get_filing_table, extract_filing_fact or search_sec_filing_text runs
confirmedRules.then: Returns INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR "Invalid SEC URL: must start with 'https://www.sec.gov/Archives/'."
confirmedRules.parameters: Allowed prefix https://www.sec.gov/Archives/ (case-sensitive)
edgeCases: http:// or upper-case variants are rejected
The Worker enforces the same prefix inline (worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:7289-7290, 8628, 8854, 8955, 9005)

confirmedRules.name: Historical price period and interval allow-lists

A domestic filer is never given an ADR ratio (line 289), so at r=2.0 > 1.5 it gets SHARE_BASIS_MISMATCH and Yahoo's count is used (lines 293-295, 300). The parameters also match: 1.9, 0.02*n, 1.5, and the regex ^(?:20|40)-F.

The card still does not describe the full behaviour:

When the SEC-to-Yahoo ratio is at most 1/1.9 (about 0.526), i.e. Yahoo's count is a near-whole multiple k of the SEC count within 2% of k, ads_ratio returns 1/k. A foreign filer then gets ADR_RATIO_APPLIED, and dividing by 1/k multiplies the SEC counts by k. The card's 'Otherwise ... SEC count is dropped' sentence predicts SHARE_BASIS_MISMATCH for this case, which is wrong for foreign filers.

2. It leaves out rounding. Shares are adjusted with round_half_up(shares / ratio) (line 298), so the result is a rounded whole number, not a plain division.

confirmedRules.name: Analyst change classification (upgrade/downgrade/initiation)

Otherwise it is classified by grade: moving into a sell-type grade is a DOWNGRADE and moving from a non-buy grade into a buy-type grade is an UPGRADE. A new grade with no prior grade is INITIATED, and anything else is MAINTAIN.

confirmedRules.name: Guidance amount scaling
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A guidance amount is scaled by its unit word (billion/bn/b = 1e9, million/mn/m = 1e6, thousand/k = 1e3) and rounded half-up to whole units. If one end of a range has no unit, it takes the other end's unit.

confirmedRules.name: Midpoint ± tolerance guidance bounds
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Guidance stated as a midpoint plus or minus a tolerance is converted to exact low/high bounds. A % tolerance is a percentage of the midpoint, basis points are hundredths of a percentage point, and a currency tolerance is taken in its own unit or else the midpoint's unit. A bare number with no $, % or unit is not read.
confirmedRules.given: 'Revenue is expected to be $3.150 billion +/- 5%' and 'gross margin 74.0%, plus or minus 50 basis points'
confirmedRules.then: Revenue low '2.9925 billion', high '3.3075 billion'; gross margin low 73.5, high 74.5
confirmedRules.parameters: bps = tolerance x 10^-2; exact decimal arithmetic, trailing zeros dropped

A tolerance without $/%/unit is ignored

confirmedRules.name: Guidance pattern precedence and GAAP basis
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Guidance patterns are tried in a fixed order: keyword-first wording, then metric-first wording, then midpoint ± tolerance, then outlook-table rows under a guidance/outlook heading within 400 characters. The first match is primary, and ranges on another basis for the same target period are kept as alternates. Basis is read from the range's own clause: non-GAAP/adjusted, GAAP, both, or not stated.
confirmedRules.given: 'GAAP diluted EPS of $5.82 to $5.92 and adjusted diluted EPS of $6.65 to $6.75 for fiscal 2026'
confirmedRules.then: Primary EPS 5.82–5.92 with basis GAAP, plus alternate 6.65–6.75 with basis NON_GAAP
confirmedRules.parameters: heading look-back 400 chars; clause look-back 200 chars; table column header 'GAAP Non-GAAP' assigns column basis; 'N/A' first cell selects the second column
edgeCases: A sentence break between heading and row disqualifies the table row
Rows for a different quarter are not alternates of a year range

confirmedRules.name: Guidance target period resolution
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A guidance range's target period is read from its own sentence first, picking the period mention closest before the range. Quarters and halves win over the fiscal year that contains them. If the sentence has none, the nearest 'outlook/guidance' mention within 1,500 characters above is used, and then the 200 characters before the range.
confirmedRules.given: 'For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, revenue is expected to be between $2.2 billion and $2.4 billion.'
confirmedRules.then: label 'Q3 2027', basis TEXT, scope SENTENCE
confirmedRules.parameters: heading look-back 1,500 chars; heading window ±100 chars; preceding window 200 chars; two-digit years +2000
edgeCases: 'fiscal year ending June 25, 2027' takes the fiscal year of that 52/53-week date (basis TEXT_PERIOD_END), then the company naming offset
No year stated: basis TEXT_YEAR_NOT_STATED, so the range is not compared

confirmedRules.name: Reported actuals labelled by period for guidance outcomes
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: SEC revenue and diluted EPS facts (10-K/10-Q, newest filing per period) are labelled by duration: 350–380 days is FY, 80–100 days is a quarter, and 170–190 days ending in June is H1. Quarters are calendar quarters only when every annual period ends in December. Otherwise they are fiscal quarters counted back from a year end whose 10-K states the fiscal year.

confirmedRules.name: Reported release metric acceptance rules
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A figure is read from release prose as a quarterly result only when its sentence has a result verb or a leading label. Sentences with guidance, award or backlog wording, sentences with ±, and annual-only sentences are skipped. Non-GAAP figures, per-share figures for totals, and figures attributed to another metric are rejected. Unscaled amounts take the release's table scale only when exactly one scale is declared. Losses and parentheses make the value negative.

'increased 5.2% to $X' reads X, never 5.2%

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A driver fact's period is INSTANT without a start date, QUARTER for 80–100 days, ANNUAL for 350–380 days, YEAR_TO_DATE for 101–349 days, and OTHER otherwise. A driver sentence with plan words only is TARGET_OR_PLAN, with actual words only is REPORTED_ACTUAL, and with both or neither is UNCLEAR.

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If chain quality is LOW, or contracts were in the band but none qualified, the hedge screen is PARTIAL and budget feasibility is unknown. Otherwise feasibility is true when at least one candidate fits the budget, and the shortfall to the cheapest candidate is reported.

confirmedRules.name: Option chain data quality grade
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An option chain is graded LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH from four shares of contracts: zero bid or ask, zero open interest, placeholder IV, and a last trade more than 5 days old. Any one share over its limit triggers that grade.

Unparseable data_date skips the staleness test

confirmedRules.name: Options flow put/call ratio and max-pain strike
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The put/call ratio is total put volume ÷ total call volume for the next expiry. Max pain is the strike where option holders would collect the least at expiry. Max pain is not given when total open interest is zero.
confirmedRules.given: Put volume 12,000, call volume 10,000
confirmedRules.then: pcRatio = 1.20; maxPainStrike = strike minimising Σ max(0,K−strike_call)×callOI + Σ max(0,strike_put−K)×putOI

edgeCases: call volume 0 gives pcRatio null
call + put OI <= 0 adds warning MAX_PAIN_UNAVAILABLE_ZERO_OI

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The 'IV percentile' places the nearest-strike call's IV within the min–max range of rolling 30-day realized volatility (annualised with √252) over the last year. It is clamped to 0–100 and left out when bars are stale or incomplete, or when most IVs are placeholders.
confirmedRules.given: ATM IV 0.45, rolling RV min 0.30, max 0.60
confirmedRules.parameters: window 30 sessions; ≥31 closes; ≥5 RV points; annualisation √252; placeholder IV ≤ 0.0001
edgeCases: rv_max == rv_min gives null
STALE daily bars add IV_PERCENTILE_UNAVAILABLE_STALE_DAILY_BARS

confirmedRules.name: Put volume proxy and window trend
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Put activity is today's put contracts ÷ 1% of the stock's 10-day average share volume. Comparing with the prior window's cached reading (T-7 vs T-14, T-2 vs T-7): above 1.1× is INCREASING, below 0.9× is DECREASING, otherwise STABLE.

confirmedRules.then: putVolPer1PctStockAdv = 1.50; ratio 1.25 > 1.1 so putVolTrend INCREASING

Other window labels never have a prior reading, so the trend is always STABLE

confirmedRules.name: Options flow advisory bracket
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: With chain quality not LOW, the bracket is UPPER when P/C ≥ 1.3, or ≥ 1.0 with puts increasing. It is LOWER when P/C ≤ 0.8 and puts are not increasing, otherwise MID. No bracket is given on LOW quality.

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Options positioning uses the first expiry strictly after today's New York date. If none exists it uses the last listed expiry.

confirmedRules.name: Analyst rating change classification
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A broker action is checked in this order. An initiation action means INITIATED; 'downgrade'/'down' means DOWNGRADE; 'upgrade'/'up' means UPGRADE. Next, a move into a sell-type grade from a non-sell grade is a DOWNGRADE, and a move into a buy-type grade from a stated non-buy grade is an UPGRADE. A new grade with no prior grade is INITIATED. Anything else is MAINTAIN.
confirmedRules.given: Action 'main', from 'Hold' to 'Buy'
confirmedRules.then: UPGRADE; action 'main', 'Buy'→'Sell' is DOWNGRADE; action 'main', ''→'Buy' is INITIATED
confirmedRules.parameters: buy set {buy, outperform, overweight, strong buy, positive, market outperform, top pick}; sell set {sell, underperform, underweight, strong sell, negative, market underperform, reduce}
edgeCases: 'Hold'→'Neutral' is MAINTAIN
A move to a sell grade with an empty from-grade is DOWNGRADE, not INITIATED

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If both targets exist, the target direction comes from comparing them; otherwise it comes from the action wording. An upgrade with a lowered target, or a downgrade with a raised one, is MIXED. Net sentiment is upgrades minus downgrades.

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The dominant rating is the bucket with the most analysts in the latest period. Upside is (mean target − price) ÷ price. A mean target below the price counts as LIKELY_STALE_OR_LAGGING if any upgrade came in the last 30 days, otherwise POSSIBLY_STALE.

target ≥ price gives CURRENT

confirmedRules.name: Credit health operational EBITDA, net debt and coverage
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Leverage uses the latest quarter's debt minus cash, divided by trailing-four-quarter operating income plus D&A. Yahoo EBITDA is used only as a fallback. Interest coverage is TTM EBIT (or EBITDA) ÷ |TTM interest|.
confirmedRules.given: Total debt $500M, cash $20M, TTM operating income $120M, TTM D&A $40M, TTM interest $50M
confirmedRules.then: net debt $480M; operational EBITDA $160M; netDebtToEbitda 3.00; interestCoverageEbit 2.40; interestCoverageEbitda 3.20
confirmedRules.parameters: TTM = sum of up to 4 latest quarters; debt row fallback order Total Debt → TotalDebt → Long Term Debt
edgeCases: Fewer than 4 quarters are summed anyway; dataQuality becomes PARTIAL
Falling back to 'Long Term Debt' leaves out current debt
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: If fewer than 4 income quarters exist, the 'TTM' sum covers fewer quarters but is still treated as annual, which understates EBITDA and coverage. It is flagged only as PARTIAL.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel split on whether this moves money / is regulatory (I read server.py:6686-6747 and the helpers above it (_safe_get, and _ttm_sum at 6649-6665).

Faithful: yes.
- Total debt is taken from the latest balance-sheet column, trying "Total Debt", then "TotalDebt", then "Long Term Debt" (line 6686). Cash comes from line 6687, and net debt is debt minus cash (line 6723).
- Every TTM figure is the sum of whichever of the newest quarters (up to 4) have a value (lines 6649-6665 and 6690-6713).
- Operational EBITDA is TTM operating income plus TTM D&A. Yahoo's EBITDA is used only when either of those is missing (lines 6728-6733).
- netDebtToEbitda = round(netDebt / operationalEbitda, 2) (line 6745). interestCoverageEbit = round(EBIT / |interest|, 2) (line 6746). interestCoverageEbitda = round(operationalEbitda / |interest|, 2) (line 6747).
- The example checks out: 500-20 = 480; 120+40 = 160; 480/160 = 3.00; 120/50 = 2.40; 160/50 = 3.20.

Things the rule card leaves out:
- The EBIT input is itself "Operating Income", with Yahoo "EBIT" only as the last fallback (lines 6693-6695).
- The plain-English line "EBIT (or EBITDA)" makes it sound like one ratio with a fallback. The code actually outputs both ratios separately, and the headline interestCoverage is the EBIT one (line 6748).
- data_quality is set to PARTIAL when fewer than 4 income quarters are available (lines 6742-6743). Fewer than 4 quarters gives a partial-year sum, not a true TTM figure.
- The cash row fallback order is not listed in the parameters.
- If cash is missing, net debt is None rather than 0.

P0 justified: no, through the compliance lens. This is an analytics output from an MCP research tool built on Yahoo Finance data. It does not move money: it places no trades and charges no fees or interest. It does not enforce any regulatory requirement. And it does not guard the integrity of any system of record. A regulator or auditor would not care if this ratio method changed silently. A user's investment judgement might change, but that makes it a core calculation for the output contract (P1). It should still be covered by the repo's Python/TS parity tests. The same applies to the debt-tier and credit-stress thresholds that use it (2.5 / 3 / 4, lines 6750-6764).

No instruction-shaped text or credentials in the cited lines. The BUG-03 comment at lines 6691-6692 describes the preference for operating income, and the code does what it says. | FIDELITY: The Given/When/Then matches server.py:6686-6747. Net debt is the latest balance-sheet column's debt minus cash (6723), using debt rows in the order Total Debt, TotalDebt, Long Term Debt (6686). Operational EBITDA is TTM operating income plus TTM D&A (6728-6730). The code falls back to the sum of Yahoo's EBITDA rows only when either of those is missing (6731-6733). Leverage is round(netDebt / operationalEbitda, 2) (6745). The EBIT coverage is round(ebit / |interest|, 2) and the EBITDA coverage uses operational EBITDA (6746-6747). The arithmetic checks out: 500-20=480, 120+40=160, 480/160=3.00, 120/50=2.40, 160/50=3.20.

Edge cases the card leaves out, which a contract should state:
(a) The EBIT input tries Operating Income first, then OperatingIncome, then Yahoo's EBIT row. Cash tries Cash And Cash Equivalents, then CashAndCashEquivalents, then Cash. D&A and interest each have their own list of fallback rows.
(b) The TTM sum adds only the non-null quarters of the first row that has any value. A sum can therefore cover 1-3 quarters, and operating income and D&A can cover different quarter counts. If fewer than 4 income columns exist, data_quality is set to PARTIAL. Missing values inside a column do not trigger it.
(c) Leverage is None if net debt is missing or operational EBITDA is exactly 0. A negative EBITDA still gives a (negative) ratio.
(d) Both coverage ratios are None if interest is None or 0. A negative interest value is handled by abs().
(e) Rounding is Python's round() on a binary float: round-half-even, with float representation effects. This matters for TS parity.

None of these contradict the card, so I rate it faithful.

P0: Not justified under the stated definition. This is a read-only analytics metric. A downstream threshold uses it (credit stress = leverage > 2.5 and EBIT coverage < 3, debt tier cutoffs 1/2.5/4), but it does not move money or enforce a regulatory requirement. It only guards data integrity in the sense of output parity between the two runtimes. It is a strong P1 calculation contract.

confirmedRules.name: Release figure scale and loss sign
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An unscaled dollar figure takes the release's table scale only when the release declares exactly one scale. With more than one, the figure is skipped. P0 is justified. This rule sets the size (a 1,000x or 1,000,000x scale) and the sign of reported revenue, net income and EPS. A mistake silently corrupts financial figures, so it guards data integrity.

The worked example is correct when traced through the code. "(in millions)" is the only scale, so the revenue figure is 54229 x 1e6 = 54,229,000,000 with scaleBasis "RELEASE_TABLE_IN_MILLIONS" (line 600). For EPS, the label "diluted net loss per share" contains "loss" and not "income"/"earnings" (line 608), so it becomes -0.12. EPS is not a money metric (line 546), so the table scale is not applied to it.

The plain-English statement is not faithful, and as a behaviour contract it would produce wrong equivalence tests:
1. Loss wording only turns a value negative for epsDiluted (lines 606-611). For money metrics like revenue, net income or free cash flow, only parentheses, an ASCII "-" or the word "negative" directly before the amount count (line 512 requires `negative\s*$` in the gap). So "net loss of $5 billion" for netIncome stays positive, even though the card says loss wording makes it negative.
2. Even for EPS, a label that names both outcomes, such as "diluted income (loss) per share", is excluded (line 608). For per-share-form matches, only the last "net income/earnings/loss" mention before the amount decides the sign (lines 610-611).
3. "Unscaled dollar figure takes the release's table scale" is wrong for EPS. EPS and gross margin never take the table scale or a scale word, and their scaleBasis is None (line 592).
4. "Exactly one scale" means one distinct unit across the whole text. Repeats are de-duplicated (lines 522-524), so two "(in millions)" headers still count as one.
5. When there are several scales, only that candidate is skipped (`continue`, line 597). The loop then tries later candidates, which may carry an explicit scale word and be accepted with scaleBasis AS_WRITTEN.
6. Rounding: floor(magnitude x scale + 0.5) is applied to the unsigned magnitude before the sign (lines 602, 613), so it is effectively half-away-from-zero on the signed value. Unscaled values are not rounded; _whole only turns 5.0 into 5. An explicit scale word like "$1.2 billion" also goes through this rounding, not only table-scaled values.
7. Only the ASCII hyphen-minus counts as a minus sign (line 495). A Unicode minus is not recognised.
8. A zero result is never negated (line 613).
