confirmedRules.given: A press release matched in range with confidence HIGH and URL, but its title, tickers and issuer don't reference the ticker or company name
confirmedRules.then: Status starts CONFIRMED, all bestEvidence relevance LOW -> status PARTIAL with warning LOW_RELEASE... code LOW_RELEVANCE_EVIDENCE.
confirmedRules.parameters: Stale cutoff 90 days (_STALE_EVENT_DAYS); official source types sec_filing, company_ir, company_ir_page, press_release, newswire, yahoo_finance_press_releases; bestEvidence top 5; retryable failure modes WORKER_SUBREQUEST_LIMIT, RATE_LIMITED, PROVIDER_TIMEOUT
edgeCases: Without start/end dates every matched item counts as in range
STALE is only reachable when a date window excludes all matches
Matched items lacking publishedAt are ignored in the stale test; if every match lacks a date, stale_only is vacuously true
SEC/company_ir source types count as HIGH relevance automatically

confirmedRules.name: Verification coverage failure-mode precedence
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When an event isn't found and sources were impaired, the reason is chosen in a fixed order: worker subrequest limit, rate limited, timeout, provider changed, Yahoo identity unavailable, unconfigured, not eligible, provider error.
confirmedRules.given: Finnhub RATE_LIMITED and Yahoo PROVIDER_ERROR, no match
confirmedRules.then: failureMode RATE_LIMITED, status SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND, retryable true.
confirmedRules.parameters: Precedence: WORKER_SUBREQUEST_LIMIT ('too many subrequests' in SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE text) > RATE_LIMITED > PROVIDER_TIMEOUT > PROVIDER_CHANGED > YAHOO_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE > SOURCE_UNCONFIGURED > SOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE > PROVIDER_ERROR
edgeCases: AUTH_ERROR and IR-page states produce no failure mode, so status stays NOT_FOUND

confirmedRules.name: News source coverage state and recommended next action
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Coverage is PARTIAL if any source is unconfigured, ineligible, errored, rate limited, timed out, changed, or an IR-page source is not registered/due for revalidation; the next action is retry (rate limit/timeout), check official releases (other failures or ineligible skips), retry the truncated source, or use the returned context.
confirmedRules.given: Finnhub status NOT_ELIGIBLE (market not enabled) and Yahoo OK
confirmedRules.then: state PARTIAL, skippedSources [finnhub], recommendedNextAction CHECK_OFFICIAL_RELEASES. NOT_NEEDED skips do not limit coverage.
confirmedRules.parameters: Action precedence RETRY_RETRYABLE_SOURCES > CHECK_OFFICIAL_RELEASES > RETRY_TRUNCATED_SOURCE > USE_RETURNED_CONTEXT
edgeCases: A resolved_action passed by the caller overrides the derived action
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: failed_states in _build_coverage (lines 315-320) includes WEBSITE_NOT_AVAILABLE, DISCOVERY_NOT_FOUND, DISCOVERY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, FEED_NOT_FOUND and PARSE_ERROR, but _compute_source_coverage (2402-2406) does not, so a response can list failedSources while reporting coverage state FULL.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should discovery/feed/parse failures make coverage PARTIAL, matching their inclusion in failedSources?

confirmedRules.name: News collection status when results are empty or limited
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A news collection with items but an unavailable/ineligible/identity-unavailable source is PARTIAL; an empty one is SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND if any source was limited or an IR-page problem occurred, NOT_FOUND if sources ran cleanly, and PROVIDER_ERROR if no source ran.
confirmedRules.given: No items returned, warning SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for Yahoo Finance
confirmedRules.then: SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND, so an empty result is not read as genuine absence.
confirmedRules.parameters: Limiting codes SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, SOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE, SOURCE_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, any COMPANY_IR_PAGE_* warning
edgeCases: Items present and no limiting warning -> status None (normal)

confirmedRules.name: Event deduplication: same title stem, day and issuer, official source preferred
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: News/event items sharing a normalized title stem (first 80 characters, ticker and boilerplate words removed), publication day and issuer are merged; the higher-priority source is kept (SEC > company IR > press release > newswire > company news > Yahoo > Marketaux > other), with the newer timestamp breaking ties and the other kept as a source reference.
confirmedRules.given: A SEC 8-K item and a Yahoo news item with the same normalized title on 2026-03-04 for the same issuer
confirmedRules.then: The SEC item is kept with the Yahoo item in sourceRefs; if their timestamps differ a TIMESTAMP_VARIANCE warning (statusImpact false) is added; results sort newest first.
confirmedRules.parameters: Title stem max 80 chars; stop terms yahoo, finance, finnhub, globenewswire, press, release, inc, corp, corporation, company, plc, ltd, llc; group id = first 16 hex of SHA-256(stem|day|issuer); priorities 0-7
edgeCases: Items with neither title stem nor date get no group and pass through undeduplicated
Different issuers on the same day/title are not merged

confirmedRules.name: News item evidence class, ticker match and decision use
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each news item is graded by source: SEC EX-99 or an approved IR page is official evidence to use; other official/wire sources say 'check official releases'; Yahoo news on material topics (earnings, guidance, contract, financing, product, regulatory, litigation) also says check official releases; everything else is context only.
confirmedRules.given: A Yahoo Finance news item with eventType 'analyst' and a Finnhub-hosted URL
confirmedRules.then: evidenceClass CONTEXTUAL_NEWS, urlProvenance PROVIDER, decisionUse CONTEXT_ONLY.
confirmedRules.parameters: Evidence classes SEC_FILING, APPROVED_IR_PAGE, OFFICIAL_RSS_ATOM, WIRE_RELEASE, CONTEXTUAL_NEWS; provider hosts finance.yahoo.com, finnhub.io; tickerMatch EXPLICIT/SOURCE_SCOPED/UNVERIFIED
edgeCases: A plain sec_filing item is only CHECK_OFFICIAL_RELEASES, not USE_OFFICIAL_EVIDENCE
Item with no URL -> urlProvenance UNKNOWN

confirmedRules.name: Event type from keywords (first matching category wins)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: News events are typed by the first keyword family found in the text (earnings, guidance, contract, financing, product, analyst, macro, litigation, insider, regulatory, other); SEC forms map directly (10-Q/10-K earnings, S-1/S-3/424B financing, 8-K/proxy regulatory, Form 4 insider).
confirmedRules.given: Headline 'Company raises $200 million in note offering'
confirmedRules.then: eventType 'guidance' because 'raises' (guidance family) is checked before 'offering' (financing family).
confirmedRules.parameters: Keyword lists as coded at lines 593-612
edgeCases: Matching is plain substring: 'steps' contains 'eps' -> earnings; 'second' contains 'sec' -> regulatory; 'notable' contains 'note' -> financing
424B4 is not mapped to financing by _event_type_from_form (exact match only)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Substring keyword matching misclassifies (e.g. 'takes steps' -> earnings, 'raises capital' -> guidance), which then drives decisionUse for Yahoo items.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should event keywords match whole words, and should 'raises/lowers' count as guidance only when paired with guidance/outlook wording?

confirmedRules.name: Ticker mention compatible with listing exchange
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A text matches a company if its ticker appears as a whole word and is not prefixed by a different exchange (e.g. 'TSXV:ABC' for a NASDAQ company); failing that, a company name alias (3+ chars) or a 3-6 letter acronym match is accepted.
confirmedRules.given: Company ABC on NASDAQ; text 'TSXV: ABC announces drilling results'
confirmedRules.then: The ticker match is rejected (incompatible exchange prefix) and the item is kept only if the issuer name or acronym appears.
confirmedRules.parameters: Exchange normalization NASDAQ/NYSE/NYSEAMERICAN/TSXV/TSX; prefix look-back 20 chars; known incompatible raw prefixes include ASX, LSE, TSX-V; acronym length 3-6; alias min length 3
edgeCases: Unknown company exchange -> any whole-word ticker hit is accepted
Unknown prefix like 'OTC:' is accepted
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: _normalize_exchange checks 'NYSE' before 'NYSE AMERICAN'/'AMEX', so 'NYSE American' (and 'NYSEArca') normalize to NYSE; also 'GS' substring maps any exchange code containing GS to NASDAQ.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should NYSE American listings be distinguished from NYSE when validating ticker prefixes?

confirmedRules.name: Marketaux wire fallback eligibility
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The quota-bounded Marketaux wire fallback runs only when the caller explicitly chose non-priority sources, or when Yahoo/Finnhub coverage was limited, or when they returned no item matching the query.
confirmedRules.given: Default sources; Yahoo returned 4 items, none containing the query 'buyback'; Finnhub completed OK
confirmedRules.then: Reason HIGHER_PRIORITY_EMPTY so Marketaux runs (max 3 items, wire domains only).
confirmedRules.parameters: Priority sources yahoo_finance, yahoo_finance_news, yahoo_finance_press_releases, finnhub; Marketaux max items 3; wire domains businesswire.com, prnewswire.com, globenewswire.com
edgeCases: No priority source selected -> EXPLICIT_SOURCE_SELECTION
A priority source not completed or in an error status -> HIGHER_PRIORITY_COVERAGE_LIMITED
Matching items present and no limits -> no fallback

confirmedRules.name: Approved company IR page URL and revalidation
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Company IR page items are accepted only from HTTPS URLs on the registry's allowed hosts (ignoring www) and allowed path prefixes; an entry is fresh until its revalidateAfter date, and an unparseable date counts as stale.
confirmedRules.given: Registry entry allowing host investors.example.com and prefix /news/; an item linking to http://investors.example.com/news/x
confirmedRules.then: Rejected (scheme not https). An https link under /news/ is accepted with confidence HIGH, approvalStatus approved.
confirmedRules.parameters: Scheme https only; www prefix stripped; revalidateAfter null -> always fresh
edgeCases: Malformed revalidateAfter -> treated as not fresh
Relative links are resolved against the final fetched URL before checking

confirmedRules.name: Event request input clamps and source allow-list
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Event/news requests clamp max results to 1-100 and lookback to 1-3,650 days; unsupported source names are dropped with a warning and, if none remain, defaults are used.
confirmedRules.given: max_results=500, lookback_days=0, sources=['twitter','sec','sec']
confirmedRules.then: max_results 100, lookback default value used (0 is falsy) then clamped >=1, sources ['sec'] with warning SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED for 'twitter'.
confirmedRules.parameters: max_results 1-100; lookback 1-3650 days; supported sources sec, company_ir, company_ir_page, newswire, yahoo_finance, yahoo_finance_news, yahoo_finance_press_releases, finnhub, marketaux
edgeCases: Duplicates removed preserving order
0 is treated as 'not given' and replaced by the default

confirmedRules.name: Material SEC filings filter and limit cap
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Material filings are those whose form equals or starts with an allowed form (default 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, S-1, 424B, DEF 14A, 20-F, 6-K) and is not a noisy form; at most 20 are returned and the response says when more exist.
confirmedRules.given: limit=120 for a filer with 35 material filings
confirmedRules.then: 20 filings returned, moreAvailable true, warning LIMIT_CAPPED stating the 20 maximum and that more filings exist.
confirmedRules.parameters: Max 20; default limit 5; noisy forms 3, 4, 5, SC 13G(/A), SC 13D(/A), 144, SD, CORRESP, UPLOAD, CT ORDER; xbrl_available if isXBRL or isInlineXBRL = 1
edgeCases: Prefix match includes amendments and variants (10-K/A, 10-KT, 8-K/A, 424B4)
limit < 1 clamps to 1

confirmedRules.name: Decision-grade SEC XBRL fact
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An extracted SEC fact is decision-grade only if it has a value, status FOUND, an XBRL extraction method, an XBRL context, and source evidence naming the source type, concept, accession number and period end.
confirmedRules.given: A revenue value FOUND via XBRL whose evidence lacks an accession number
confirmedRules.then: Not decision-grade (false).
confirmedRules.parameters: Required evidence fields sourceType, concept, accessionNumber, periodEnd
edgeCases: HTML-table or text-extracted values are never decision-grade under this test

confirmedRules.name: Geographic revenue table selection and share check
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A region's revenue share is read from a filing table that names the region and is about revenue (not square footage or assets); geographic-breakdown tables are preferred; the region cannot exceed the total, and a table's own '% of total' figure must agree within 1 percentage point.
confirmedRules.given: Table titled 'Revenue by geographic region' with China 150 and Total 1,000 (in millions) and a '% of total' column showing 16.5%
confirmedRules.then: Computed share 15.0% differs from stated 16.5% by 1.5 pts > 1.0, so the table is rejected; without the stated column the result is pct 0.15, usd 150,000,000, denominator 1,000,000,000.
confirmedRules.parameters: Stated-pct tolerance 1.0 pt; region <= total x 1.001; tables scanned max 800; lead-in window 1,500 chars (last 800 used); geographic score 2 vs 1; China aliases include PRC, mainland china, country:cn, srt:chinamember
edgeCases: A total row must carry amounts; otherwise the last numeric row is used
A % beside a value counts as a share only under a '% of'/'percent of' header (not a Change column)
Dash cells read as 0

confirmedRules.name: Automatic 20-F fallback for geographic and segment revenue
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a 10-K revenue extraction returns NOT_DISCLOSED/no rows and the company has ever filed a 20-F, extraction is retried on the 20-F; success replaces the result with an AUTO_20F_FALLBACK note, failure adds a POSSIBLE_20F_FILER warning.
confirmedRules.given: Ticker TSM, region 'Taiwan', filing_type 10-K, which returns NOT_DISCLOSED
confirmedRules.then: The 20-F is read; if a value is found the output is replaced (status FOUND) with info warning AUTO_20F_FALLBACK; otherwise POSSIBLE_20F_FILER is added.
confirmedRules.parameters: Trigger: filing_type 10-K and confidence NOT_DISCLOSED (geo) or zero segment rows; 20-F detection: any '20-F' in recent submissions forms
edgeCases: Missing region -> INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR payload with confidence NOT_DISCLOSED
valueRatio/valuePct withheld when no denominator; DENOMINATOR_NOT_FOUND warning added
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: On fallback success, confidence defaults to HIGH when the 20-F payload gives none (line 9631), whereas the primary path defaults to NOT_DISCLOSED.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should a 20-F fallback value with no stated confidence default to HIGH?

confirmedRules.name: Guidance history run status and retryability
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Guidance history reads up to 12 (default 8) recent 8-K Item 2.02 earnings releases; its status is NO_EARNINGS_RELEASES_FOUND, RELEASE_TEXT_NOT_AVAILABLE (all unread), PARTIAL (some unread or actuals unread) or OK, and unread releases are never treated as withdrawn guidance.
confirmedRules.given: 8 releases picked, 2 unreadable, companyfacts readable
confirmedRules.then: status PARTIAL, retryable true, warning RELEASE_TEXT_NOT_AVAILABLE '2 of 8 ... missing, not withdrawn'.
confirmedRules.parameters: max_releases clamp 1-12, default 8; read batch size 4; only form 8-K with '2.02' in items (8-K/A only on request)
edgeCases: No CIK and ticker index readable -> NO_SEC_REGISTRANT (not retryable); index unreadable -> SEC_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE (retryable)
Companyfacts unreadable -> ACTUALS_NOT_READ warning, outcomes not evaluated

confirmedRules.name: Operating driver ledger status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The operating driver ledger is PARTIAL when the filing text, companyfacts or the earnings release could not be read; a truncated filing read or no resolved release alone keeps it OK.
confirmedRules.given: Filing read but truncated; companyfacts read; release status RELEASE_NOT_RESOLVED
confirmedRules.then: status OK, warnings FILING_READ_TRUNCATED and RELEASE_NOT_RESOLVED, retryable false.
confirmedRules.parameters: Non-degrading warnings FILING_READ_TRUNCATED, RELEASE_NOT_RESOLVED
edgeCases: Release NOT_READ -> PARTIAL and retryable

confirmedRules.name: Valuation evidence pack composition guards
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The evidence pack runs the dilution bridge only with a current price in a USD listing (minor-unit prices converted first), retries guidance once if the release text failed, and marks consensus LIMITED when every provider returned no periods.
confirmedRules.given: A London listing quoted 250 GBp
confirmedRules.then: Major price 2.50 GBP; dilution component NOT_APPLICABLE with code NON_USD_LISTING; quote component OK.
confirmedRules.parameters: Minor units GBp/GBX->GBP /100, ZAc->ZAR /100, ILA->ILS /100; horizon_years 1-5; material filings limit 10
edgeCases: No price -> dilution PRICE_UNAVAILABLE and quote FAILED
Only one guidance retry, sequential

confirmedRules.name: Stock screener count cap and name allow-list
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Screeners must be one of the predefined names and return at most 250 results; ticker search with exchange 'US' keeps only NASDAQ (NMS), NYSE (NYQ) and NYSE Arca (PCX).
confirmedRules.given: screen_stocks('day_gainers', count=1000)
confirmedRules.then: count reduced to 250.
confirmedRules.parameters: Max count 250; US exchange set {NMS, NYQ, PCX}
edgeCases: count <= 0 is not validated
US filter excludes NYSE American (ASE) and NASDAQ NGM/NCM codes
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The 'US' exchange filter omits NASDAQ Global Market (NGM), Capital Market (NCM) and NYSE American (ASE) listings.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the 'US' filter include all NASDAQ tiers and NYSE American?

confirmedRules.name: Funding text item amount status and forced UNRESOLVED
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each funding sentence gets its first dollar amount or low-to-high range. A figure under $100,000 with no scale word is marked 'scale not stated'. A sentence with no amount is kept only if it names a strong obligation, and then it is marked UNRESOLVED.
confirmedRules.given: Sentence 'We have committed $550.0 to the new facility' (no million/billion)
confirmedRules.then: amountStatus = SCALE_NOT_STATED, low/high null, classification stays COMPANY_DISCLOSED_COMMITTED. A sentence like 'We have non-cancellable purchase commitments' with no amount gets classification UNRESOLVED and unresolvedReason 'no amount stated'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Scale threshold $100,000; sentence length 40-1200 chars; sentences ending ';' skipped; up to 25 items; dedupe on first 200 chars lower-cased; qualifier 'up to' / 'approximately' read from up to 24 chars before the amount; two amounts count as a range only when joined by to/-/and AND low <= high
edgeCases: 'committed $1.2 billion and $300 million' is two amounts, not a range, because the second is smaller
'$X per share' amounts are skipped
Currency is always USD when an amount is found
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A SCALE_NOT_STATED item keeps its stated classification (for example COMMITTED) with null amounts. It is not moved to UNRESOLVED, even though no usable amount exists.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should an item whose amount scale cannot be read (SCALE_NOT_STATED) be classified UNRESOLVED like an item with no amount, or keep its stated type?

confirmedRules.name: Funding text timing horizon precedence
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The timing of a funding statement comes from the first matching pattern, in this order: a named quarter, Qn YYYY, next 12 months, remainder of the year, a year range, 'through/by YYYY', a single year. If none matches, timing is UNSTATED.
confirmedRules.given: Sentence 'We expect to pay $400 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2027 and through 2028'
confirmedRules.then: horizon=quarter, year=2027, quarter=3 (the quarter pattern wins over 'through 2028')
confirmedRules.parameters: Pattern order fixed as listed
edgeCases: No date wording gives basis UNSTATED

confirmedRules.name: Contractual obligation schedule buckets and schedule status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Debt principal, operating and finance lease payments, purchase obligations and contractual obligations are read from untagged-dimension XBRL facts at the period end, one value per due bucket. Purchase commitments are grouped by category, and a tagged min/max pair becomes a range. The schedule is COMPUTED when anything was found, otherwise NOT_FOUND.
confirmedRules.given: Period end 2026-06-30 with LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInYearTwo = $500M
confirmedRules.then: A CONTRACTUAL row: family debt_principal, bucket year_2, periodThrough 2028-06-30, amount 500,000,000. Status COMPUTED.
confirmedRules.parameters: Bucket offsets 0..6; periodThrough set only for offsets 1-5 (period end + offset years); first concept per bucket wins (purchase-obligation duplicates on anniversary concepts skipped); liquidity: cash, short-term investments (COMPANY_DISCLOSED_BALANCE), undrawn facility (CONTRACTUAL_AVAILABILITY), ATM remaining (AVAILABLE_AT_COMPANY_DISCRETION)
edgeCases: No facts at all gives warning NO_INLINE_XBRL
Facts present but no contractual rows gives info warning NO_TAGGED_SCHEDULES
Nothing is netted or summed across classifications
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: _add_years only replaces the year string. A Feb 29 period end plus 1 year produces an invalid date such as '2025-02-29'.

confirmedRules.name: Fiscal year of a period end (one-week drift rule)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The fiscal year a period belongs to is the calendar year of the date 7 days before its end date. A 52/53-week year that ends in the first week of January therefore counts as the prior year.
confirmedRules.given: A fiscal year ending 2027-01-02
confirmedRules.then: Year = 2026 (2027-01-02 minus 7 days = 2026-12-26), label FY2026. A year ending 2027-01-08 is FY2027.
confirmedRules.parameters: WEEK_DRIFT_DAYS = 7
edgeCases: Non-ISO or invalid date returns None
Companies that name years by start year (DG) need the naming offset rule to correct this

confirmedRules.name: Fiscal quarter of a period end
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A period's fiscal quarter is counted back from the fiscal year end in 91-day steps. It must fall within 10 days of a quarter boundary and within the same year, otherwise the quarter is unknown.
confirmedRules.given: Fiscal year end 2026-12-26 and period end 2026-06-27 (gap 182 days)
confirmedRules.then: quarters_left = round(182/91) = 2, so Q2
confirmedRules.parameters: Quarter length 91 days; boundary tolerance 7+3 = 10 days; gap allowed -7..280 days
edgeCases: Gap above 280 days or below -7 days returns None
Gap off a boundary by more than 10 days returns None

confirmedRules.name: Company fiscal-year naming offset
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The company's own naming of fiscal years is learned from its last three 10-K annual reports. If all three show the same offset from the period-end rule, and that offset is at most 1 year, it is applied. Otherwise the period-end rule is used with offset 0.
confirmedRules.given: DG 10-Ks: year ended 2026-01-30 stated fy 2025, 2025-01-31 stated 2024, 2024-02-02 stated 2023
confirmedRules.then: Each offset is -1 (stated year minus rule year). Result offset -1, basis SEC_STATED_FISCAL_YEAR.
confirmedRules.parameters: Reports considered: 3; annual duration 350-380 days; concepts Revenues, RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, SalesRevenueNet, NetIncomeLoss, EarningsPerShareDiluted; forms starting '10-K' with fp=FY
edgeCases: companyfacts not read: offset 0, basis PERIOD_END_RULE_SEC_NOT_READ
No stated year: PERIOD_END_RULE_NO_STATED_YEAR
Offsets disagree or |offset| > 1: PERIOD_END_RULE_STATED_YEARS_INCONSISTENT, offset 0
20-F/40-F filers are not read for naming (10-K only)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: 20-F and 40-F filers are not used to learn fiscal-year naming. Is that intended for foreign private issuers?

confirmedRules.name: Fiscal calendar pattern detection and settling
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The company's year-end rule (month end, weekday nearest the month end, or last such weekday of the month) is kept only if it reproduces every recent annual period end. Older years are added one at a time until a single rule remains, and the look-back stops at a year no rule fits.
confirmedRules.then: For 2023-2025 both WEEKDAY_NEAREST_MONTH_END and LAST_WEEKDAY_OF_MONTH fit. Adding 2020-09-03 leaves only WEEKDAY_NEAREST_MONTH_END, weekday Thursday, month 8.
confirmedRules.parameters: Minimum 2 period ends; nearest-weekday window ±3 days; MONTH_END checked first and used alone if it fits
edgeCases: Nominal months differ: no calendar
A changed calendar ends the look-back and keeps the last calendar that fit

confirmedRules.name: Projecting the company's fiscal year end from a provider date
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A provider's nominal year-end date is converted to the company's actual year end using the settled calendar. No date is projected when the month differs or when the fitting rules give different dates.
confirmedRules.given: Calendar WEEKDAY_NEAREST_MONTH_END, Friday, January; provider says 2027-01-31
confirmedRules.then: Returns 2027-01-29
confirmedRules.parameters: Uses nominal (end - 7 days) month to match the calendar month
edgeCases: Two patterns give different dates: None
No calendar or no provider date: None

confirmedRules.name: Filing fiscal-year label with mistag guard
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A filing's fiscal-year label is the year it tags for itself (dei:DocumentFiscalYearFocus), unless that tag is more than 1 year away from the period-end rule. In that case the tag is treated as a mistag and the rule year is used.
confirmedRules.given: 10-K with report date 2026-01-30 and DocumentFiscalYearFocus 2025
confirmedRules.then: FY2025 (rule year 2026, difference 1, within tolerance). If the tag were 2023, label FY2026.
confirmedRules.parameters: Tolerance 1 year
edgeCases: Untagged filing (8-K, older HTML) uses the rule year
No report date and a tag present: the tag is used

confirmedRules.name: Capital structure summary status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The capital-structure result is COMPUTED when both cash and total debt were found, PARTIAL when only some of cash, debt or instrument rows were found, and NOT_FOUND when none were.
confirmedRules.given: A filing tags cash of $1.2B but no total-debt concept, and lists two debt instruments
confirmedRules.then: status = PARTIAL
confirmedRules.parameters: none
edgeCases: Cash tagged only under a restricted-cash-inclusive concept adds info warning CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED
No inline XBRL adds warning NO_INLINE_XBRL

confirmedRules.name: Dilution bridge status and diluted share formula
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Diluted shares at the caller's price = basic + incremental shares from options, unvested awards, warrants, convertible debt and convertible preferred. The bridge is NOT_FOUND without a basic share count. It is PARTIAL if any component or class is unresolved or any open share claim exists, otherwise COMPUTED.
confirmedRules.given: Basic 100,000,000; option incremental 2,000,000; warrant incremental 3,000,000; no open claims
confirmedRules.then: dilutedSharesAtPrice 105,000,000; dilutionPctAtPrice 5.00; status COMPUTED
confirmedRules.parameters: Rounding half-up (shares to 0 dp, percentages to 2 dp); gross count adds full options outstanding, unvested awards, warrants outstanding and if-converted shares; ATM shares reported separately in dilutedSharesAtPriceWithAtm
edgeCases: No basic shares: status NOT_FOUND, bridge null, error warning BASIC_SHARES_NOT_FOUND
A component with null incrementalShares is 'unresolved'; one with unresolvedClasses/Instruments > 0 is 'partiallyResolved'
COMPUTED covers tagged instruments only, not a full claim inventory
Strike currency different from the price currency adds warning PRICE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH

confirmedRules.name: Antidilutive table reconciliation and claim promotion
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Rows in the company's antidilutive-securities table are matched by label to bridge components. Rows no component models become REPORTED_NOT_MODELED claims with the company's count. A text claim of the same kind moves from UNQUANTIFIED to REPORTED_NOT_MODELED and takes on the count.
confirmedRules.given: Antidilutive table lists 'Series A convertible preferred' 21,800,000 shares, no convertible_preferred component, and the text scan found an UNQUANTIFIED CONVERTIBLE_PREFERRED claim
confirmedRules.then: The text claim's status becomes REPORTED_NOT_MODELED with reportedShares 21,800,000. Both UNQUANTIFIED and REPORTED_NOT_MODELED count as open claims, so the bridge is PARTIAL.
confirmedRules.parameters: Rows with shares <= 0 ignored; equity_compensation is modeled if either stock_options or unvested_share_awards is present
edgeCases: Unmatched label: category 'other', kind OTHER_REPORTED_SECURITY
Nothing from the table is added to any share count

confirmedRules.name: Warrant count vs reported antidilutive count gap warning
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If the bridge's warrant count differs from the company's reported antidilutive warrant count by more than 5% of the reported count or 100,000 shares, whichever is larger, the bridge warns that a warrant class may be stale or untagged.
confirmedRules.given: Reported warrants 10,000,000; bridge warrants 9,400,000
confirmedRules.then: Gap 600,000 > max(500,000, 100,000), so warning WARRANT_COUNT_DIFFERS_FROM_REPORTED
confirmedRules.parameters: Relative tolerance 5%; absolute floor 100,000 shares
edgeCases: The reported table may be a weighted average
Only when reported warrants > 0 and a warrants component exists

confirmedRules.name: Warrants tagged after the period end are quoted, not counted
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Warrant counts the report tags after its period end (and that are not exercise or equity-movement events) are listed as UNQUANTIFIED WARRANT_AFTER_PERIOD_END claims, with their exercise price. They are never counted as outstanding.

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A tagged conversion ratio is accepted as shares per $1,000 if ratio × price ÷ 1,000 ≈ 1. If ratio × price ≈ 1 it was tagged per $1 and is scaled by 1,000. Any other value is rejected as not the conversion rate.

Any cash-settled note unresolved makes the component's net-share total null

confirmedRules.name: Analyst valuation method extraction status and subject attribution
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Valuation methods named in news are context only. Status is FOUND if any item names a method, METHOD_NOT_DISCLOSED if there are only targets or rating changes, otherwise NOT_FOUND. When issuer names are supplied, a sentence must be about the subject or it is rejected.

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A Companies House search result matches an issuer only on an exact normalised name match (ignoring PLC, LIMITED, LTD, HOLDING(S), GROUP, THE, and '&' read as AND). Among exact matches an active company is preferred, otherwise the first exact match is used.

confirmedRules.then: Ratio r = 5.00, nearest whole n = 5, |r-n| <= 2% x 5, so ADR ratio 5 applies; basic shares used = 5,186,000,000 and an ADR_RATIO_APPLIED info warning is added

The Given/When/Then is right, but the plain-English text and parameter list overstate or leave out several edge cases. Fix these before the rule becomes a contract:

The check looks for any undimensioned fact from that accession, at any date and in any unit, for any of the many concepts in capital_structure._BORROWING_CONCEPTS (capital_structure.py:2426-2430). confirmedRules.parameters: _SEC_YAHOO_EXCESS=0.10; _SEC_YAHOO_CASH_MATCH=0.02; _SEC_YAHOO_SHORTFALL=0.05; _SAME_QUARTER_DAYS=7
edgeCases: Both are flags only; values are not overridden
Yahoo cash is ignored for the check when currencies are not comparable

confirmedRules.name: Valuation snapshot enterprise value and status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Enterprise value = price x diluted shares + debt - principal of convertibles counted as shares (capped at debt) + liquidation preference of convertible preferred not counted as shares - cash - short-term investments. Status is COMPUTED when EV exists, else PARTIAL.
confirmedRules.given: Price $20, diluted 110M shares, debt $600M including a $300M convertible counted as shares, cash $200M, STI $100M, no preferred
confirmedRules.then: EV = 2,200M + 600M - 300M - 200M - 100M = $2,200M; status COMPUTED
confirmedRules.parameters: Formula string at valuation.py:452-453
edgeCases: No price at all -> status PRICE_UNAVAILABLE
Currency not comparable and Yahoo balances -> ENTERPRISE_VALUE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH, EV null
Preferred with no liquidation preference -> PREFERRED_NOT_IN_ENTERPRISE_VALUE warning
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The convertible principal is taken out of debt whenever the bridge shows incrementalShares > 0, even when sec_usable is false. In that case diluted shares are null and Yahoo's basic count is used, so the convertible is removed from debt without being added to shares. The preferred adjustment does check sec_usable.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: When the SEC share count is rejected (SHARE_BASIS_MISMATCH), should convertible principal still be removed from debt?

confirmedRules.name: Multiples suppressed for currency mismatch or non-positive denominators
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: EV/Revenue, EV/EBITDA and P/E are computed only when the financial currency matches the quote's major currency (GBp/GBX->GBP, ZAc->ZAR, ILA->ILS at 1/100) and the denominator is positive. Each multiple is rounded to 2 dp.
confirmedRules.given: A UK listing quoted at 250 GBp with GBP financials and trailing EPS of 0.20
confirmedRules.then: Major price 2.50 GBP; P/E = 12.50. For a TWD-financials / USD-quote listing every multiple is null with a 'different currency' note; a negative EBITDA gives a null multiple with a 'not meaningful' note
confirmedRules.parameters: Minor units: GBp,GBX,ZAc,ILA divisor 100; periods 0y=current FY, +1y=next FY

confirmedRules.name: Peer median comparison excludes the subject
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Peer medians are taken over the peers only (the subject is excluded). The subject's premium is (own/median - 1) x 100, computed only for multiples (not percentage metrics) and only when the median is positive.
confirmedRules.given: Peer EV/Revenue values 4, 6, 10 and subject 9
confirmedRules.then: Median 6; subject premium = 50.00%. For grossMarginPct no premium is computed

confirmedRules.name: LTM flow metric = LFY + YTD - prior YTD
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The last fiscal year is the latest 350-380 day period. LTM equals LFY when nothing later is filed. Otherwise LTM = LFY + the year-to-date starting 0-4 days after LFY ends - the prior-year YTD (starting within 4 days of LFY start, ending 358-372 days before the current YTD, length within 7 days of it).
confirmedRules.given: LFY revenue to 2024-12-31 $1,000M, 9-month YTD to 2025-09-30 $900M, prior 9-month YTD to 2024-09-30 $700M
confirmedRules.then: LTM = 1,000 + 900 - 700 = $1,200M, method LFY_PLUS_YTD_MINUS_PRIOR_YTD
confirmedRules.parameters: Annual 350-380 days; YTD start gap 0-4 days; prior-year end gap 358-372 days; span tolerance 7 days
edgeCases: No annual period -> NOT_AVAILABLE NO_ANNUAL_PERIOD_FILED
No matching YTD -> YEAR_TO_DATE_NOT_FILED
No prior YTD -> PRIOR_YEAR_TO_DATE_NOT_FILED
Several YTD candidates -> the longest wins

confirmedRules.name: Point-in-time fact selection and concept precedence
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Historical valuation uses only 10-K/10-Q/20-F/40-F facts filed on or before the date. For each period the earlier-listed concept wins. A later filing replaces an earlier one only for the same concept, never with a lower-priority alternate concept.
confirmedRules.given: Revenue for FY2024 tagged as ...ExcludingAssessedTax in a 10-K filed 2025-02-15 and as Revenues in a 10-K/A filed 2025-04-01
confirmedRules.then: The ...ExcludingAssessedTax value is kept, and facts filed after 2025-05-01 are ignored

confirmedRules.name: Staleness limits by SEC filing cadence
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For a filer whose latest annual report by the date is a 20-F/40-F, share counts, balances and results go stale after 500 days. Otherwise share counts go stale after 400 days, balances after 200 and results after 500. An annual filer's count older than 183 days is still used but flagged.
confirmedRules.given: A 10-Q filer whose latest balance sheet is 230 days before the valuation date
confirmedRules.then: EV status BALANCES_STALE (value null) and a BALANCES_STALE warning. For a 20-F filer with a share count 300 days old, market cap is computed with a SHARE_COUNT_AGED info warning
confirmedRules.parameters: ANNUAL: 500/500/500; QUARTERLY: share 400, balances 200, results 500; SHARE_COUNT_AGED_DAYS=183
edgeCases: The cadence is judged per date, so a filer that changed regime keeps its earlier cadence
A stale denominator sets the multiple status to RESULTS_STALE

confirmedRules.name: Historical market cap status precedence
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Price is the close within 7 days on or before the date, with later splits undone. Market cap is then OK only when a positive point-in-time share count exists, is not stale, and no split falls between the count date and the trading date.
confirmedRules.given: Close $10 adjusted for a later 4-for-1 split, cover-page count 50,000,000 as of 90 days earlier, no split in between
confirmedRules.then: Unadjusted close = 40.00; market cap = $2,000,000,000 (status OK)
confirmedRules.parameters: Status order: PRICE_UNAVAILABLE (no close within 7 days) > SHARES_NOT_AVAILABLE > SHARE_COUNT_NOT_POSITIVE > POINT_IN_TIME_SHARES_UNRESOLVED (weighted-average only) > SPLIT_AFTER_SHARE_COUNT > SHARE_COUNT_STALE > OK
edgeCases: A count of 0 is shown but gives no market cap
A weighted-average basic count is shown but never sets market cap
An ADR count is divided by the ADS ratio

confirmedRules.name: Point-in-time share count source order
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The share count is taken from the undimensioned cover page, then the balance sheet. The latest periodic filing's own cover-page count (or class sum) replaces it when that read is OK and newer. A weighted-average count is used only as unusable context.
confirmedRules.given: Companyfacts cover count as of 2024-10-31 and a 10-K filed 2025-02-20 whose cover read is OK as of 2025-02-10
confirmedRules.then: The 10-K cover count as of 2025-02-10 is used

confirmedRules.name: Cover-page share count read status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Reading dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding from a filing fails as a whole if any context or value cannot be read. At the latest date an undimensioned count wins; otherwise per-class counts are summed only when each fact has exactly one dimension and it is the class-of-stock axis.
confirmedRules.given: Class A 400,000,000 and Class B 100,000,000, each on ClassOfStockAxis only
confirmedRules.then: status OK, value 500,000,000, basis COVER_PAGE_CLASS_SUM (and the SHARE_CLASSES_SUMMED info warning downstream)
confirmedRules.parameters: Status precedence: CONTEXT_NOT_READ > VALUE_NOT_PARSED > NOT_TAGGED > OK / OTHER_DIMENSIONS
edgeCases: A zero/dash format or a dash text is read as 0
A comma-decimal format is honoured

confirmedRules.name: Historical EV status precedence and no-borrowings rule
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Balances are read at the latest cash date, with no carry-forward. Debt is the first tagged debt group plus short-term borrowings/commercial paper. Debt is 0 when the filing that reported the cash tags no borrowing concept at all. EV = market cap + (debt - cash - STI) x FX.
confirmedRules.given: Market cap $2,000M, cash $300M, STI untagged, filing tags no borrowing concept, FX 1
confirmedRules.then: Debt = 0 (NO_BORROWINGS_TAGGED info); EV = $1,700M, with a SHORT_TERM_INVESTMENTS_NOT_TAGGED info warning
confirmedRules.parameters: Status order: MARKET_CAP_NOT_AVAILABLE > BALANCES_NOT_AVAILABLE > DEBT_NOT_TAGGED > FX_NOT_AVAILABLE > BALANCES_STALE > OK
edgeCases: IFRS has no borrowingConcepts, so the zero-debt rule never applies
An FX rate must be within 7 days on or before the date

confirmedRules.name: Historical multiple status and EBITDA construction
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each multiple is numerator / (denominator x FX), to 2 dp. It is null with a status when the numerator, denominator or FX is missing, or either side is non-positive. EBITDA = operating income + D&A for the same period end; depreciation alone is used when amortization was never tagged.
confirmedRules.given: EV $5,000M, LTM operating income $300M and D&A $100M ending the same day, FX 1
confirmedRules.then: EBITDA $400M; EV/EBITDA = 12.50. A negative EV gives NOT_MEANINGFUL_NONPOSITIVE_NUMERATOR
confirmedRules.parameters: Status order: <NUMERATOR>_NOT_AVAILABLE > DENOMINATOR_NOT_AVAILABLE > FX_NOT_AVAILABLE > NOT_MEANINGFUL_NONPOSITIVE_NUMERATOR > NOT_MEANINGFUL_NONPOSITIVE_DENOMINATOR > OK
edgeCases: Different period ends -> EBITDA NOT_AVAILABLE PERIODS_DIFFER
Separate D&A parts must all be OK for the same period (PARTS_NOT_ALIGNED)

confirmedRules.name: Historical valuation point and run status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A date's status is OK only when market cap, EV and all eight multiples (4 multiples x LTM/LFY) are usable. coreStatus covers market cap and EV only. The run is OK only when every date is OK, and FUNDAMENTALS_NOT_AVAILABLE when there are no revenue facts.
confirmedRules.given: A date with market cap and EV OK but P/E null because of negative net income
confirmedRules.then: status PARTIAL, coreStatus OK, coverage 7 of 8 available, with the unavailable multiple listed
confirmedRules.parameters: _MULTIPLE_NAMES=evToRevenue, evToEbitda, priceToEarnings, priceToSales; cadence MIXED when dates differ

confirmedRules.name: Reporting currency and taxonomy per date
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: us-gaap is used when it carries revenue, else ifrs-full. The main currency is the revenue unit with the most facts. At each date the currency is that of the newest annual revenue fact filed by then, with the main currency preferred on ties.
confirmedRules.given: An IFRS filer with 40 TWD and 4 USD revenue facts whose latest 20-F tags both
confirmedRules.when: The currency for a date is resolved
confirmedRules.then: TWD

confirmedRules.name: Default historical valuation dates
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Callers may request up to 12 YYYY-MM-DD dates (deduplicated and sorted). Without a request, the latest close and its anniversaries over the previous five years are used, with 29 February falling back to the 28th.
confirmedRules.given: Latest close 2024-02-29 and no dates requested
confirmedRules.parameters: MAX_DATES=12; 5 anniversary years

confirmedRules.name: Stale provider snapshot fallback
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A provider's stored daily snapshot may stand in for a live request only when the live failure is RATE_LIMIT, TIMEOUT or PROVIDER_ERROR. It must match the provider, operation and ticker, and be no more than 7 days old and not later than as-of. It never stands in for a missing key or entitlement.
confirmedRules.given: An Alpha Vantage RATE_LIMIT at 2025-06-10T12:00Z and a matching snapshot fetched 2025-06-09T05:30Z
confirmedRules.then: The snapshot is used with staleFallback ageHours 30.5. The PROVIDER_DATA_STALE warning is raised downstream
confirmedRules.parameters: STALE_FALLBACK_MAX_AGE_DAYS=7; statuses RATE_LIMIT, TIMEOUT, PROVIDER_ERROR
edgeCases: UNCONFIGURED/AUTH failures never fall back
A snapshot dated in the future relative to as-of is rejected

confirmedRules.name: Consensus provider cell state
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A provider's estimate is not covered when it has no mean (or 0 analysts). It is inconsistent when the mean is outside its own high-low or low > high. It has insufficient analysts below 3. Otherwise it is covered.
confirmedRules.given: Alpha Vantage revenue mean 667.6M, high 652.7M, 12 analysts
confirmedRules.then: state PROVIDER_INCONSISTENT (MEAN_ABOVE_HIGH); the row is shown but left out of the agreement check, with a PROVIDER_ROW_INCONSISTENT warning
confirmedRules.parameters: minAnalystCount=3; tolerance 1e-9 x max(1,|v|)

confirmedRules.name: Provider agreement classification
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Usable provider means are compared. Fiscal year ends more than 10 days apart are a period mismatch, and differing currencies a currency mismatch. Identical figures at the coarsest published precision with the same analyst counts are IDENTICAL (not independent). Otherwise the cell is AGREED within 10% relative (or $0.02 absolute for EPS), else CONFLICT.
confirmedRules.given: EPS means 5.20 (Yahoo) and 5.30 (Alpha Vantage), same fiscal year end and currency, different analyst counts
confirmedRules.then: Absolute diff 0.10 > 0.02; relative = 0.10/5.30 = 1.89% <= 10%, so the cell is AGREED
confirmedRules.parameters: conflictTolerancePct=10; epsAbsoluteTolerance=0.02; period identity 10 days; horizon 1-5 years (default 5)
edgeCases: No usable rows but some inconsistent -> PROVIDER_INCONSISTENT
One usable row -> SINGLE_PROVIDER

confirmedRules.name: EPS gap explained by an unadjusted split
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A conflicting EPS pair is relabelled NOT_SPLIT_ADJUSTED when the ratio between the two means is within 15% of a split (or cumulative splits) of at least 1.5x in the prior 400 days. The provider on the pre-split basis is named.
confirmedRules.given: EPS 2.92 vs 0.73 and a 4-for-1 split 100 days earlier
confirmedRules.then: gap 4.0 matches 4 -> NOT_SPLIT_ADJUSTED; the provider with 2.92 is named not adjusted
confirmedRules.parameters: SPLIT_LOOKBACK_DAYS=400; SPLIT_RATIO_TOLERANCE=0.15; minimum factor 1.5; exactly two providers; same sign

confirmedRules.name: Consensus metric coverage and cross-check status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each cell's coverage is NOT_COVERED, INCONSISTENT, CONFLICT (conflict, period/currency mismatch or not split-adjusted), INSUFFICIENT_ANALYST_COUNT, or COVERED. The curve as a whole is NO_PROVIDER, SINGLE_PROVIDER, NOT_COMPARED, NOT_INDEPENDENT (every compared cell identical) or CROSS_CHECKED.
confirmedRules.given: Yahoo and Alpha Vantage both OK, 4 cells compared, all IDENTICAL
confirmedRules.then: status NOT_INDEPENDENT with a PROVIDERS_NOT_INDEPENDENT warning. Each failed provider (status not OK and not NO_DATA) adds CROSS_CHECK_DEGRADED

confirmedRules.name: FY0 resolution and fiscal-year offset
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: FY0 is Yahoo's '0y' fiscal year when stated, else the earliest provider fiscal year ending on or after the as-of date. Later years are numbered by rounding (days between year ends)/365.25.
confirmedRules.given: FY0 ending 2025-01-31 and a provider year ending 2026-01-30
confirmedRules.then: 364/365.25 rounds to 1 -> FY+1

confirmedRules.name: EPS revision window state
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For each 7/30/60/90-day window the state is NOT_REPORTED (missing past or current), then PROVIDER_INCONSISTENT, then SPLIT_IN_WINDOW (a split within days+1), else COMPARED with change and change%.
confirmedRules.given: Current EPS 3.00 and 30-day-ago 2.50, no split
confirmedRules.then: 30d change 0.50, changePct 20.00, state COMPARED. A 4-for-1 split 20 days ago makes the 30d/60d/90d windows SPLIT_IN_WINDOW with no change
confirmedRules.parameters: Windows 7,30,60,90 days; split lookback 91 days; one day of margin

confirmedRules.name: Evidence family readiness states and blockers
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Preflight grades each evidence family. Quote: READY, or STALE after 4 days; UNAVAILABLE (retryable) on provider failure; MISSING otherwise. Periodic filing: STALE after 135 days, or 492 days for 20-F/40-F filers. Guidance: STALE 120 days after the latest Item 2.02 8-K. Consensus: READY/PARTIAL/MISSING by FY0/FY+1 cells covered, or UNAVAILABLE when every provider failed.
confirmedRules.given: A 10-Q filer whose latest 10-Q covers a period 150 days ago, and a quote 2 days old
confirmedRules.then: quote READY; secPeriodicFiling STALE with blocker SEC_PERIODIC_STALE; capitalStructure/dilution READY_TO_EXTRACT (PARTIAL if the filing is not inline XBRL)
confirmedRules.parameters: Quote 4 days; QUARTERLY_REPORT_STALE_DAYS=135; ANNUAL_REPORT_STALE_DAYS=492; guidance 120 days; material 8-K window 90 days; PROVIDER_FAILURE_STATUSES={PROVIDER_ERROR,RATE_LIMIT,PROVIDER_TIMEOUT,ERROR,TIMEOUT}
edgeCases: Filings list None -> UNAVAILABLE rather than MISSING
Consensus failure gives one retryable CONSENSUS_PROVIDER_ERROR instead of per-cell blockers

confirmedRules.name: Evidence cut component status and receipt coverage
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each sub-tool result is FAILED (error, no response, non-JSON or ok=false), LIMITED (its status contains PARTIAL, INCOMPLETE, STALE, NOT_AVAILABLE, NOT_FOUND, UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED, NO_DATA, NOT_DISCLOSED, UNCONFIGURED or FAILED) or OK. The receipt is COMPLETE if all are OK, FAILED if none are, else PARTIAL.
confirmedRules.given: Five components where one returns status PARTIAL
confirmedRules.then: That component is LIMITED; coverage okCount 4, state PARTIAL, evidenceCompleteness NOT_ASSERTED
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The LIMITED regex is a substring match, so for example 'NOT_FOUND' also matches statuses like 'PERIOD_NOT_FOUND' (intended) but would also match any future status containing these fragments.

confirmedRules.name: Evidence write-once storage lifecycle
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Evidence cuts and consensus observations are written once under fixed keys. The write returns UNAVAILABLE without a configured store, ALREADY_STORED if the key exists (never overwritten), STORED on success, FAILED on error, and never fails the research call.
confirmedRules.given: An evidence cut key already present on disk
confirmedRules.then: status ALREADY_STORED and the file is unchanged
confirmedRules.parameters: Keys must match ^(evidence-cuts|consensus-history)/[A-Za-z0-9._^=/-]+\.json$ with no '..'

confirmedRules.name: Equivalent-concept fact selection by newest filing
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a fact can come from several equivalent concepts, the concept with the most recently filed fact of the requested form wins. The earlier-listed concept wins ties, unless on_tie='larger' picks the larger newest-period magnitude. A pinned accession limits facts to that filing.
confirmedRules.given: Revenue as ...ExcludingAssessedTax last filed 2023-02-28 and ...IncludingAssessedTax filed 2025-02-27
confirmedRules.then: ...IncludingAssessedTax is selected
confirmedRules.parameters: REVENUE_CONCEPTS order: ExcludingAssessedTax, IncludingAssessedTax, Revenues, SalesRevenueNet

confirmedRules.name: A filing's own fact value: latest end, shortest period
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A filing's own value for a fact is the first listed concept tagged in that accession, at its latest period end, using the shortest period there. A 10-Q therefore gives the quarter, not the year to date.
confirmedRules.given: A 10-Q tagging revenue for a 3-month and a 9-month period both ending 2025-09-30
confirmedRules.then: The 3-month value is returned
edgeCases: Instant facts (no start) count as duration 0
Unparseable dates count as very long periods

confirmedRules.name: Named fiscal-year period parsing and row selection
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A requested period must be 'latest', 'FY2025' or '2025'; anything else is refused. A fiscal year matches a period's issuer year: the fy of the first filing that reported it with fp=FY, if within one year below the period-end year (end date less 7 days); else that period-end year. The newest-filed rows come first.
confirmedRules.given: A period ending 2026-01-02 first reported with fy=2025, fp=FY
confirmedRules.then: The rows match (2026-01-02 less 7 days falls in 2025); 'FY 2025x' would be refused with the help text

confirmedRules.name: Ticker, accession and SEC URL format validation
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Tickers must be 1-20 characters of uppercase letters, digits or . - ^ = (after trim and uppercase). Accession numbers must be NNNNNNNNNN-NN-NNNNNN. SEC document URLs must start with https://www.sec.gov/Archives/.
confirmedRules.given: Ticker 'brk.b' and accession '0000320193-24-000123'
confirmedRules.then: Both pass ('BRK.B'); 'AAPL$' would be rejected

rejectedRules.name: Options max-pain strike
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: Max pain is the strike at which the total intrinsic payout to option holders at expiry is smallest. For each strike S it sums (S − call strike)+ × call OI plus (put strike − S)+ × put OI.
rejectedRules.given: Calls: 100 strike OI 10, 110 strike OI 5; Puts: 100 strike OI 8, 90 strike OI 4
rejectedRules.when: Max pain is computed over strikes {90,100,110}
rejectedRules.parameters: Summary tool suppresses max pain when total OI <= 0 OR more than 50% of contracts have zero OI
edgeCases: Ties keep the lowest strike (strict <)
Majority-zero-OI chain gives MAX_PAIN_UNAVAILABLE_ZERO_OI
rejectedRules.suspectedDefect: get_options_flow_scan (server.py:7712) suppresses max pain only when total OI is zero, not when most contracts have zero OI, so the two tools can disagree on the same chain.
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The formula in the rule and the suppression guard both match the code. The worked example does not: the code gives a different max-pain strike from the same inputs.

What matches, in /home/user/yahoo-finance-mcp/server.py:
- Line 3904 builds the candidate strikes from the call and put strikes combined.
- Lines 3918-3924 add up (S - call strike) clipped at zero times call OI, plus (put strike - S) clipped at zero times put OI, for each strike S. They keep the first strike with the strictly smallest total, so ties go to the lower strike.
- Lines 3907-3915 skip the calculation and add warning MAX_PAIN_UNAVAILABLE_ZERO_OI when total OI is zero or less, or when more than half of the contracts have OI of zero or less (missing OI counts as zero).

The example worked through with the code's logic:
- S=90: call payout 0; put payout (100-90)x8 + 0 = 80. Total 80.
- S=100: call payout 0; put payout 0. Total 0.
- S=110: call payout (110-100)x10 = 100; put payout 0. Total 100.

So the code returns maxPainStrike = 100, not 90. The rule's figures of 100 at S=100 and 280 at S=110 do not follow from the rule's own formula. This is a P1 calculation rule, so a wrong Then-clause would make any test or port built from it fail.

Suggested fix: change the example to "Payouts: 90 gives 80; 100 gives 0; 110 gives 100. maxPainStrike = 100". It could also note that ties go to the lowest strike.

rejectedRules.name: Expanded institutional ownership provider fallback
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: Finnhub is tried first unless the ticker or its suffix is on the ineligible list. Scarce Alpha Vantage quota is used only when the caller sets allow_scarce_fallback and Finnhub gave no usable rows. Holders are capped at 1–100 (default 50), and results are never decision-grade.
rejectedRules.given: Ticker 'XYZ.BK' with an ineligible suffix, allow_scarce_fallback=false
rejectedRules.then: Finnhub NOT_ELIGIBLE, no Alpha call, status NOT_FOUND, action VERIFY_SEC_13F_OR_ENABLE_SCARCE_FALLBACK
rejectedRules.parameters: max_holders 1-100 default 50; ownership TTL 7 days; eligibility list in worker/src/news-source-capabilities.json
edgeCases: Unreadable eligibility policy file: Finnhub treated as eligible
Response symbol mismatch: rows discarded
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: Most of the rule matches the code, but the one scenario it gives as its specification produces a different result than the rule says.

What matches:
- The eligibility check lowercases nothing and compares in upper case: it looks up the ticker in the ineligible list and checks the suffix list from worker/src/news-source-capabilities.json (provider_gaps.py:217-226; the path is set at line 27).
- If the policy file fails to load, the ticker is treated as eligible (line 221).
- Finnhub is called only for eligible tickers (lines 310-316).
- Alpha Vantage is called only when no usable rows came back and allow_scarce_fallback is true (line 341).
- max_holders must be 1 to 100, default 50 (lines 297 and 303-304).
- The cache lifetime is 7 days (line 24).
- Successful results have decisionGrade False (line 417).

What does not match: the specification's Then clause. For 'XYZ.BK' with an ineligible suffix and fallback off, line 318 creates a result whose status is "NOT_ELIGIBLE" (the second field of ProviderJsonResult is status, per yfmcp/clients/market_providers.py:31-39). Line 367 keeps any status that is not OK, so the status stays NOT_ELIGIBLE and does not become NOT_FOUND. The special VERIFY_SEC_13F_OR_ENABLE_SCARCE_FALLBACK action applies only when the status is NOT_FOUND (lines 369-370). So the action comes from _recovery_for("NOT_ELIGIBLE"), which returns USE_YAHOO_OR_OFFICIAL_FILINGS (lines 68-69). The real output is status NOT_ELIGIBLE with action USE_YAHOO_OR_OFFICIAL_FILINGS, not NOT_FOUND with VERIFY_SEC_13F_OR_ENABLE_SCARCE_FALLBACK. The rest of that scenario is correct: Finnhub's attempt is recorded as NOT_ELIGIBLE and Alpha Vantage is not called.

Smaller issue: the failure payload's decisionGrade field was not checked, because _provider_failure_payload was read only up to line 89. "Never decision-grade" is confirmed only for the success path.
